The approach is demonstrated by deriving an explicit inverse formula for the mixed mass matrix of the eight-node hexahedral element. This formula enables efficient element-level inversion without solving a global system. The proposed method can improve inertial representation in transient dynamic analyses while retaining the computational advantages of explicit time integration and is suitable for element-by-element implementations.

papers.title: Hill's Lunar Equation as a Leaf: Riccati Reduction and Frobenius Theory for Second-Order PDEs
papers.abstract: The equations of Hill and Adams for the lunar perigee and node, Mathieu's equation and Lamé's equation arise as leafwise restrictions of one class of linear partial differential equations, the \emph{square-type foliated equations} $L^2u+A\,Lu+B\,u=0$, where $L$ is an analytic vector field and $A,B$ are analytic functions. Such an equation has a regular singularity exactly when the foliation defined by $L$ is analytically linearizable. At rational saddles, where every point of the indicial conic is resonant, we obtain convergent solutions whose exponents are holomorphic functions of a first integral; their variation describes the monodromy along the leaves and decides when classical Frobenius solutions exist. For a Hill equation, the characteristic exponent becomes the value of such a holomorphic function, given by a convergent series. This yields rigorous computer-assisted proofs of Hill's constant for the motion of the lunar perigee and of Adams' constant for the motion of the node: Hill's value is confirmed within his own error estimate and its fifteenth decimal is determined, his value of the motion of the perigee is shown to be correct in all its digits, and Adams' value is confirmed to twelve decimals. For Mathieu's equation, the curves of constant characteristic exponent that govern ion trapping appear as classical Frobenius loci. For Lamé's equation, we prove a product formula for the logarithmic obstructions, which coincide with the leading coefficients of the eigenvalue splittings computed by Volkmer and whose vanishing reflects the finite-gap property.

papers.title: C*-algebras constructed using acyclic groups
papers.abstract: We show that the free group on countably many generators is not $C^\ast$-superrigid. Furthermore, we realize each of $O_{\infty}$ and the Jiang-Su algebra as a crossed product of a commutative $C^\ast$-algebra. Finally, we construct non-trivial, outer actions on classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras whose crossed products exhaust all classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras. The common theme in the proofs is the use of torsion-free, acyclic groups.

papers.title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
papers.abstract: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

papers.title: The Sharp Holder Constant in Mori's Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $K\ge 1$ and let $f$ be a $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ onto itself with $f(0)=0$. We prove that $\lvert f(a)-f(b)\rvert\le 16^{1-\frac{1}{K}}\lvert a-b\rvert^{\frac{1}{K}}$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb{D}$. The constant is sharp, confirming the conjectured value of the Mori constant. The proof reduces the estimate along a Beltrami path to an infinitesimal inequality, which follows from quasiconformal distortion bounds and a three-pole integral estimate.

papers.title: Bounded functions on the character variety for quadratic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: For any finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, Schneider--Teitelbaum defined and studied the character variety in $p$-adic Fourier theory. It is a rigid analytic curve over $L$ that parameterizes the set of locally $L$-analytic characters of $o_L$. It is conjectured that all bounded functions on the character variety of Schneider--Teitelbaum come from $p$-adic measures. We prove this conjecture for all quadratic extensions $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$.

papers.title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
papers.abstract: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-ε)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

papers.title: Microwave-optical quantum transduction with quantum-well exciton polaritons
papers.abstract: Linking superconducting quantum processors over optical fiber requires microwave-optical quantum transducers that are efficient, high-bandwidth, and low-noise. This combination has been out of reach because of the weak nonlinearities of conventional electro-optic (EO) materials. We propose a transducer with an engineered, strong EO nonlinearity using the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) of quantum-well excitons. The QCSE transducer leverages the strong light-matter interactions and extreme polarizability of quantum well excitons. Strong coupling to an optical cavity forms exciton-polaritons whose vacuum EO coupling is up to five orders of magnitude larger than in a typical thin-film lithium niobate device. We describe a GaAs/AlGaAs stepped-quantum-well transducer design with predicted transduction efficiencies above 60% and fewer than 0.01 added noise quanta over a $\sim$60 MHz bandwidth, using pump powers below 10 $μ$W and loaded optical and microwave quality factors of only $3\times10^4$ and $10^3$. We further show that the cavity protection of the polariton provides robustness against inhomogeneous broadening of the quantum well excitons.

papers.title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
papers.abstract: Preserving quantum states in the presence of environmental decoherence remains a fundamental challenge for quantum information processing. This work investigates whether Hamiltonian Lyapunov feedback can transiently preserve the state of an open qubit by reshaping its trajectory under Markovian dissipation. A state-error Lyapunov function is adopted to derive an analytical feedback law for Lindblad dynamics, ensuring a nonincreasing Lyapunov function whenever the control sensitivities are nonzero. The analysis identifies the geometric conditions under which the feedback becomes ineffective, showing that control authority vanishes when the current and target Bloch vectors are collinear. Numerical simulations are performed for amplitude damping and pure dephasing using selected target states. Performance is evaluated through fidelity, accumulated infidelity, dwell time above a fidelity threshold, coherence, and control effort. The results demonstrate that the proposed feedback cannot eliminate irreversible dissipation or achieve universal asymptotic stabilization, but it can provide transient benefits for selected target-channel combinations. In particular, under amplitude damping, the controller significantly reduces accumulated infidelity and substantially extends the interval during which the system remains above a prescribed fidelity threshold. In the pure dephasing cases examined, improvements in fidelity are generally limited, although transient coherence preservation is observed for the oblique target considered, revealing a trade-off between coherence and state fidelity. These findings indicate that Lyapunov-based Hamiltonian feedback is best suited as a transient preservation mechanism and motivate its application to gate operations and preservation of prepared states during finite time intervals before their use or readout.

papers.title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
papers.abstract: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $ρ$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

papers.title: Boxes in Infinite Words: Complexity, Automata, and Point Modules
papers.abstract: Motivated by the geometry of point modules over monomial algebras, we introduce a box-counting function associated to a right-infinite word over a finite alphabet. An extendable box is a family of finite words obtained by choosing letters independently at each position, subject to the condition that all choices admit a common infinite right continuation in the associated subshift. We prove several results for these functions for words of linearly bounded complexity. For $k$-automatic words, we show using techniques from first-order logic that the total box-counting function is $k$-regular. Finally, we apply our results to prove eventual affine growth of the number of positive-dimensional irreducible components in finite projections of point-module spaces associated to semiprime monomial algebras of at most quadratic growth.

papers.title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.

papers.title: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Protecting quantum coherence is a central theme of modern quantum technologies. Carefully designed control pulses can extend coherence by suppressing disorder and unwanted interactions. However, designing robust pulse sequences remains challenging in interacting multi-level systems, where multiple independent error channels must be controlled in the presence of experimental imperfections. Here we introduce QORA, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework that integrates theoretical reasoning, automated experimental calibration and control for closed-loop discovery of quantum control sequences. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, QORA discovers AID-ROD, a series of AI-discovered sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time relative to the state-of-the-art human-designed sequence DROID-C3PO. Subsequence analysis by human researchers reveals a hierarchy of error suppression: 18-pulse blocks suppress linear and quadratic onsite disorder and common-mode drive-amplitude errors, while their arrangement over a longer cycle reduces dipolar interactions, providing a physical explanation for the observed improvement and robustness in AID-ROD. These results demonstrate AI-guided experimental discovery of robust quantum control and identify a design strategy for protecting coherence in interacting multi-level systems beyond qubits.

papers.title: Restoring quantum neural network trainability through reusable calibration
papers.abstract: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) rely on measured quantum observables to guide optimization, but hardware noise can suppress the parameter-dependent signals essential for learning. Here, we develop a structure-preserving error-mitigation framework that improves QNN trainability through reusable calibration of the quantum circuit's effective noise response. By calibrating a reference circuit with the same gate architecture as the trainable circuit, we construct regularized estimators of local quantum features that remain fixed throughout training. We quantify how calibration errors and response mismatches affect the recovery of both observables and their derivatives. Numerical simulations demonstrate enhanced loss-landscape contrast, faster convergence, and improved classification performance, and an IBM Quantum experiment confirms improved closed-loop variational optimization under hardware noise. We further demonstrate calibration reuse in a modular QNN comprising 25 independent four-qubit channels, corresponding to 100 qubits in aggregate. Our results establish reusable feature calibration as a practical approach to improving noise-limited quantum machine learning without repeated calibration at every training step.

papers.title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal Čech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

papers.title: Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moiré Systems
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moiré superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $ν_B=1$ in the presence of a moiré superlattice potential, with three electrons per moiré cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moiré bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moiré minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a Néel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.

papers.title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
papers.abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
papers.abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlevé V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.

papers.title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding
papers.abstract: The python's lunch conjecture relates the complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks to an exponential cost associated with post-selection. We establish a tight query lower bound for this decoding problem in a Haar random oracle model, with a python's lunch circuit that applies Haar random unitary $U$ to a logical input and fixed ancillas, followed by post-selection on $m$ output qubits. Given one copy of the normalized encoded state and coherent oracle access to $U$ and $U^\dagger$, including controlled queries, we prove that recovering even a single logical bit with constant average advantage requires $Ω(2^{m/2})$ queries. Together with the state-independent amplitude amplification upper bound for approximately isometric encodings, this establishes query complexity $Θ(2^{m/2})$ at constant decoding accuracy. We also comment on the decoding cost for other "admissible'" ensembles of unitaries $U$ which give rise to families of approximately isometric holographic maps.

papers.title: Limited-Memory First-Order Methods: Identification, Reconstruction, $H$-Duality and Application to Optimized Methods
papers.abstract: In general, linear-span first-order methods add at every iteration a combination of all observed gradients to the previous iterate. However, many methods of interest can be implemented in a way that requires storing only a few auxiliary vectors, instead of all past gradients. We call such methods limited-memory first-order methods. A given fixed-coefficient first-order method can be described by a lower triangular coefficient matrix, which expresses each step as a combination of previous gradients. We show that the minimum number of running sums required to implement a method is equal to the minimum rank of a completion of the strict lower triangular part of its coefficient matrix, and propose a reconstruction algorithm. Moreover, taking the $H$-dual of a method, which reflects the coefficient matrix across its anti-diagonal, preserves its memory and translates into a permutation and time-reversal on the coefficients of the running sum recurrences. We apply our results to two optimized first-order methods for smooth strongly convex functions. First, our reconstruction applied to a method numerically designed by Shu and Wang reveals a recurrence with one auxiliary vector, which is related to the Triple Momentum Method (TMM) of Van Scoy, Freeman and Lynch with a particular initialization. We prove that the reconstructed method, called TMM-GD, is minimax optimal at every horizon for the final distance to the minimizer relative to the initial gradient norm. Second, the Information-Theoretic Exact Method (ITEM) of Taylor and Drori, optimal for the final distance relative to the initial one, is known to be memory one. We give an explicit recurrence with one auxiliary vector for its $H$-dual, called ITEM-GG, and prove that ITEM-GG is the unique minimax optimal nonadaptive linear-span method for the final gradient norm relative to the initial one.

papers.title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
papers.abstract: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value $T_0$. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches $T_0$. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.

papers.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
papers.abstract: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification problem as co-NP-complete, filling a key gap in the literature. Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-art verifiers.

papers.title: QEDist: Practical Exact Distance Certification for Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: We present QEDist, a method and software package that certifies the distance of qubit stabilizer codes. Building on tree-search methods, QEDist constructs candidate logical operators one qubit at a time, using sparse parity checks, stabilizer equivalence, and verified symmetries to reduce the work. For a cutoff $W$, a completed search either finds a nontrivial logical operator of weight at most $W$ or proves that none exists. Because satisfying one check can violate another, we use both satisfied and unsatisfied checks to lower-bound the weight needed to complete a logical operator, and prune branches whose bound exceeds the remaining budget, which substantially reduces net search time. We benchmark QEDist mainly on Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes; the same formulation extends to non-CSS codes and to the fault distance of syndrome-extraction circuits. For lifted-product (LP) codes, we further exploit the product structure to replace part of the full-code search with a smaller search on a classical constituent. We establish exact distances for codes with up to several thousand qubits, including Abelian and non-Abelian LP codes whose distances were previously reported only as upper bounds. In several seconds of search on one laptop core, QEDist certifies exact distances up to 20 for many of these codes and fault distance 10 for the syndrome-extraction circuit of the $[[144,12,12]]$ code. With orders-of-magnitude speedups over the tested exact solvers, QEDist makes exact distance certification a practical tool for selecting and optimizing finite-length quantum codes.

papers.title: Exceptional cubics on 7-manifolds
papers.abstract: A $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ on a $7$-manifold $\mathcal M$ determines a two-dimensional space of invariant totally symmetric cubic forms on each fiber of the rank-$27$ bundle $S^2_0T^*\mathcal M$ of traceless symmetric $2$-tensors. This space is spanned by the trace cubic $C_0$ and a cubic $C_\varphi$ that, up to a constant factor, is the pointwise integrand of the Yukawa coupling on the $G_2$ moduli space. We determine the exact infinitesimal stabilizers over $\mathbb C$ of all nonzero cubics in this family. For $C_0+λC_\varphi$, the stabilizer has dimension $78$ precisely at the two non-real values $λ_\pm=(1\pm i\sqrt7)/8$. Its dimension is $21$ for $C_0$ and $14$ in all other cases. At $λ_\pm$, the stabilizer is simple of type $E_6$, and the corresponding cubic is linearly equivalent to the complex Albert algebra cubic norm. The two cubics at $λ_\pm$, which we call critical, define complex-conjugate $E_6$-reductions of the complexified bundle. At any element with nonzero critical norm, the corresponding cubic determines a complex Albert algebra with basepoint stabilizer $F_4$; a line subbundle of the tangent bundle selects a smooth bundle of these algebras with tensorial operations and a Euclidean real form. The induced Levi-Civita connection preserves either critical cubic exactly when the $G_2$-structure is torsion-free. Its orthogonal projections onto the two exceptional reductions coincide with the connection induced by the minimal $G_2$-connection.

papers.title: Hyperbolic systems with non-diagonalisable principal part and variable multiplicities, IV: time-dependent characteristics, representation of solutions and regularity
papers.abstract: We consider first-order linear hyperbolic systems with time-dependent pseudo-differential principal symbols and characteristic roots of variable multiplicity. Building on the time-independent work of Kamotski and the first author, we introduce a finite-type condition along the lifted bicharacteristic flow that accounts for the contact of time-dependent characteristic roots. Under this condition, we construct a representation of solutions using time-dependent Fourier integral operators and a Picard series whose terms become increasingly smooth. This leads to an asymptotic expansion in smoothness and local \(L^p\) regularity estimates with the expected loss of derivatives. We also apply these results to higher-order scalar weakly hyperbolic equations with involutive characteristics and time-dependent principal symbols. Finally, we consider upper triangular systems with possibly non-diagonalisable principal parts and derive a representation formula involving integrated Fourier integral operators. This extends the earlier results of Garetto, Jäh and the first author to time-dependent principal parts.

papers.title: Quantum Cohomology and irrationality of Küchle fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove that very general Küchle fourfolds of types (c1), (c6), (b8), and (b11) are irrational. The key ingredients are a new rationality criterion, based on the theory of Hodge atoms due to Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu and its integral extension by Guéré, and a computation of the action of quantum multiplication on the vanishing cohomology of these fourfolds, which uses a version of the Quantum Lefschetz Hyperplane Principle. Quantum multiplication acts as a scalar on the vanishing cohomology, and we give an enumerative interpretation of this scalar.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Grad's conjecture of any knot type
papers.abstract: We construct smooth magnetohydrostatic counterexamples to Grad's conjecture in toroidal domains of arbitrary knot type. The magnetic field is nonvanishing, and nested pressure tori fill the domain outside a nondegenerate magnetic axis. The equilibria have trivial Euclidean symmetry group and occur in smooth families of inequivalent configurations. On each regular pressure torus the magnetic flow is smoothly conjugate to a linear flow with any prescribed positive constant slope. A variation of this argument gives equilibria of arbitrary knot type with twist (that is, nonconstant rotational transform) and any finite regularity. A key ingredient of the proof is a deformation method that creates knot topology from axial symmetry by separating the sheets of a covering immersion into a braid, which may be useful in other deformation problems.

papers.title: On strongly pseudoconvex Kähler--Berwald manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the equivalence between the Kähler--Finsler and Kähler--Berwald conditions for complex Finsler metrics. That is, a Kähler--Finsler metric always satisfies the complex Berwald condition: its Chern--Finsler nonlinear connection reduces to the Chern connection of a Kähler metric. We also provide, for the first time, smooth weakly Kähler--Finsler examples which are not Kähler--Berwald; and propose a condition that is formally stronger than weakly Kähler--Finsler, with equivalence holding in complex dimension two. Then we prove the de Rham decomposition and uniformization theorems for Kähler--Berwald manifolds, and show that every strongly pseudoconvex locally symmetric complex Finsler metric is both Kähler--Berwald and complex Einstein--Finsler. Additionally, we establish several rigidity theorems for the Kobayashi and Carathéodory metrics: $F_K$ is Kähler--Berwald if and only if it is Kähler; if the manifold is simply connected, then $F_C$ is Kähler--Berwald if and only if it is Kähler.

papers.title: Fourier Algebras of HLS Groupoids: Lifts, Amenability, and Spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the Fourier algebra of a certain class of groupoids, called the HLS groupoids, within Paterson's continuous framework for locally compact groupoids. We develop the basic harmonic analysis of HLS groupoids by obtaining concrete descriptions of their topology, representations, and Fourier algebra. We then study the restriction maps from the Fourier algebra $A(\mathcal{G})$ of an HLS groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ to the Fourier algebras of its isotropy subgroups, and construct explicit norm-preserving lifts for these restriction maps. As applications, we describe the norm of every element of $A(\mathcal{G})$ in terms of the norms of its restrictions to the isotropy subgroups. We prove an analogue of Leptin's theorem characterizing when $A(\mathcal{G})$ has a bounded approximate identity. We also show that the Gelfand spectrum of $A(\mathcal{G})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathcal{G}$. Finally, using abstract arguments that, unlike our methods for HLS groupoids, do not yield explicit constructions, we show that norm-preserving lifts exist and that the Gelfand spectrum of the Fourier algebra is homeomorphic to the groupoid for every étale groupoid. This generalizes Eymard's theorem and answers a question of Paterson for étale groupoids.

papers.title: Trustworthy Numerical Software in the Age of AI: What Would Turing Do?
papers.abstract: AI coding agents can now produce numerical software faster than human experts can review it, raising serious concerns about usability and reliability. These and other AI tools are already transforming mathematics and software, and they will soon transform mathematical software. These concerns motivated us to assess AI-generated numerical linear algebra (NLA) kernels, which we did through an audit of a recent public GPU QR competition. All five leading kernels passed the competition's accuracy tests, and the winning kernel achieved a 107-fold speedup over the competition's baseline, which calls NVIDIA's QR routine. Yet each failed at least once on new inputs, even those from the competition's generator, under the same checker, while the baseline passed them all. In light of this, we want to develop reusable formalizations of numerical analysis methods, which remain sparsely represented in existing formal libraries. We describe VSCL, our Lean library of mathematical foundations for numerical computing. We also propose VERNA to connect these tasks by using formalized results to guide kernel assessment against explicit specifications. Drawing on Turing's work on rounding-error analysis and program checking, we discuss design principles for developing trustworthy numerical software when direct human checking is impractical.

papers.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part II: Tameness of Motivic Measures
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with the study of the fixed-genus asymptotics of motivic measures of moduli spaces of stable pointed curves and their minimal all-light Hassett compactifications as the number of markings tends to infinity. A motivic wall-crossing argument gives a universal change of variables between the two generating series, depending only on the value of the Lefschetz class. For an arbitrary motivic measure, we use stabilization graphs and support patterns to express the all-light series in terms of universal chain factors and finite residual quotient families. This formal decomposition isolates the rational trivalent contribution without requiring a fixed-locus formula for finite quotients. To pass from formal identities to asymptotics, we formulate analytic hypotheses (the $\mathrm{H}_g$-hypotheses) for scalar realizations with positive real Lefschetz value. We introduce vertex tameness and residual-quotient tameness, whose conjunction, graph tameness, provides geometric sufficient conditions for the $\mathrm{H}_g$-hypotheses. In genus at least two, this yields explicit leading asymptotics in both chambers, depending only on the genus and the Lefschetz value; genera zero and one are treated separately. As an application, we prove graph tameness for Hodge-Deligne evaluations and deduce fixed-product universality and asymptotic concentration of Hodge numbers on the diagonal.

papers.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
papers.abstract: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $Ω(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $Θ(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size. In contrast, Laplacian perfect state transfer costs at least $Ω(2^{d/2})$ edges when the distance partition of vertices around one vertex is almost equitable. Finally, we show that Laplacian peak state transfer in trees requires $Ω(d!)$ edges, and we characterize all trees of diameter $\leq 4$ admitting Laplacian peak state transfer, thus answering a pair of questions posed by Coutinho, Guo, and Schmeits.

papers.title: Second scaling regime in high-dimensional function approximation and curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: High-dimensional function approximation is often subject to the curse of dimensionality, commonly described by a hypercube scaling regime with a large expense of $R^d$ grid points, where $R$ denotes the side length of a hypercube in $d$ dimensions. Here we show that a second scaling regime, which we call the lattice ball scaling regime, also arises and is relevant for practical applications. In this regime, the expense scales as $d^{R^2}/(R^2!)$ and therefore grows polynomially with $d$. This regime arises without additional special assumptions of special types of function spaces or error norms. The lattice ball scaling regime occurs when $R^2\ll d$, due to the discrete nature of counting the expense as the number of lattice points inside a hypersphere. Here we investigate this regime, which arises from the classical problem of approximating high-dimensional functions from common spaces of analytic or $m$-times continuously differentiable functions using orthogonal series (spectral method) such as Fourier, Chebyshev, and Legendre polynomial series. For many applications, the expense in the lattice ball scaling regime can be substantially smaller than that of the hypercube scaling regime, making accurate approximations more accessible. Numerical illustrations include classifying images of handwritten digits from the MNIST dataset and learning the solution operators of partial differential equations, such as Burgers' equation and the radiative transfer equation. The potential for connections with artificial neural networks and other machine learning methods is also discussed.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution. However, existing approaches largely focus on improving general measurement capabilities, often overlooking the structure of specific sensing tasks and leaving potential performance gains untapped. Here, we develop an algorithmic approach to quantum sensing tailored to various spectroscopic tasks, providing new avenues for improvement. Specifically, we consider general time-varying signals supported on a known set of $N$ candidate frequencies, a setting we call discrete-frequency spectroscopy. We formulate three types of practically motivated sensing tasks---Detection, Search, and Learning---that require progressively more spectral information. For all tasks, we design optimal quantum sensing algorithms achieving a $\sqrt{N}$ speedup over conventional frequency-scanning approaches. Optimal Detection and Search need only a single-qubit sensor under $π$-pulse control, whereas optimal Learning provably requires coherent processing with a quantum computer. End-to-end numerical simulations incorporating various experimental imperfections predict up to two-orders-of-magnitude speedup in Detection. As an example, we analyze the feasibility of our Detection and Search algorithms for real-world molecular screening based on state-of-the-art nitrogen-vacancy centers. We also show how quantum-computing-enhanced Learning enables wireless communication in a weak-signal regime where conventional methods fail. Our results establish a practical route toward realizing quantum advantages via designing task-specific sensing algorithms.

papers.title: Regular subgroups of wreath products and Cayley Cartesian products
papers.abstract: The Cartesian product of Cayley graphs is again a Cayley graph. For connected graphs, the converse question reduces to Cartesian powers of Cartesian-prime graphs, and consequently to the study of regular subgroups of wreath products in the product action. We prove that, for a transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $2p$ or $4p$, where $p$ is prime, $G\wr S_2$ contains a regular subgroup if and only if $G$ does, and construct counterexamples of degree $8p$ for every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$. By modifying this construction, we obtain an infinite family of connected non-Cayley graphs whose Cartesian squares are Cayley graphs, giving a negative answer to the converse question. The smallest graph in our family has $120$ vertices and valency $27$. In contrast, we prove that a connected vertex-transitive graph of order $pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are primes, has a Cayley Cartesian power if and only if the graph itself is Cayley.

papers.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. In this work, we present a rigorous benchmark of variational quantum recurrent neural networks (QRNNs) on time series prediction tasks, focusing on two key capabilities: memory and nonlinear processing. We introduce a task-driven methodology that quantifies model capacity, enabling an intuitive and fair comparison across architectures, including classical recurrent baselines. We evaluate the proposed framework on two generic benchmark tasks and on a synthetic dataset describing a chaotic system. Overall, the quantum models achieve performance comparable to their classical counterparts, but classical models scale better with the memory size within the range studied. Notably, one QRNN variant shows higher average capacity on the task designed to jointly probe memory and nonlinear capacity. Moreover, our results show that quantum models offer better capacity when we are able to find a good parameter initialization. However, the increasing sensitivity to initialization leads to a lower probability of finding good solutions as the model size increases. These results provide a principled starting point for designing richer quantum recurrent architectures and for assessing where they may offer practical benefits.

papers.title: Complex Moments of the Derivative of the Riemann Zeta Function
papers.abstract: We investigate the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function through a random Euler product model. For each fixed $σ>1/2$ and every $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$, we show, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, that the $2s$-th moment of $|ζ'(σ+\mathrm{i}t)|$ over $t\in[1,T]$ converges, as $T\to\infty$, to the corresponding moment of the derivative of the random Euler product. We then establish, unconditionally, an asymptotic formula for the latter moment as $σ\downarrow 1/2$ throughout the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. For positive real moments, our approach is based on a change-of-measure argument and a Gaussian limit theorem for the logarithmic derivative under a tilted probability measure. For general complex moments, we combine Fourier analysis of weighted complex measures with regularized Riesz distributions. As an application, under the Lindelöf hypothesis, we resolve the conjecture of Simm and Wei [J. Lond. Math. Soc. 113 (2026)] on the complex moments of the derivative of the Riemann zeta function for every $s\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s)>0$. We establish the predicted asymptotic formula as $σ\downarrow1/2$, with the leading order $s^2+2s$ and an explicit leading coefficient involving an arithmetic factor and the confluent hypergeometric function of the first kind. The conjecture also holds unconditionally when $\operatorname{Re}(s)\in (0,2)$.

papers.title: Axioms for relative entropy
papers.abstract: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.

papers.title: Large gaps and the ten martini problem for monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove the ten martini theorem for a large class of monotone potentials. The key strategy is to establish polynomially large gaps for periodic approximations.

papers.title: The cost of enforcing long-run coverage: a phase transition in online conformal prediction
papers.abstract: Consider an online prediction setting, where at each time, we are given a new feature vector and asked to provide a prediction interval or prediction set that will likely contain the corresponding response. In this setting, if the data points are i.i.d. (or more generally, exchangeable), conformal prediction provides a mechanism for building valid prediction sets around the output of any trained model, offering coverage probability $\geq 1-α$ at each time $t$. In practice, however, issues such as distribution drift, changepoints, or other challenges may cause violations of the i.i.d. assumption. In this adversarial setting, online conformal prediction methods can still offer guarantees on long-run empirical coverage. However, there is a trade-off between these two types of goals: enforcing tight constraints on long-run empirical coverage to protect against the adversarial setting can lead to unstable oscillations in the instantaneous training-conditional coverage in the i.i.d. setting. In this work, we seek best-of-both-worlds algorithms that aim to minimize cumulative error in instantaneous training-conditional coverage when in the i.i.d. setting, while also offering long-run empirical coverage guarantees in the adversarial setting. Specifically, consider a condition that requires long-run empirical coverage to deviate from the target level $1-α$ by at most $\mathcal{O}(T^{-β})$, for some $β\in[0,1]$. We prove that this family of conditions can be described with a phase transition. For $β\in[0,\frac{1}{2}]$, it is possible to construct algorithms satisfying such a constraint in the adversarial setting, while offering the same instantaneous coverage performance as split conformal prediction if the data is in fact i.i.d. On the other hand, for $β\in(\frac{1}{2},1]$, this type of condition comes at a cost, and does not achieve best-of-both-worlds behavior.

papers.title: The Sum of Leaf Weights in the Minimum Spanning Tree of the Complete Graph
papers.abstract: Let $G_n$ be a random weighted complete graph on $n$ vertices, where edges have i.i.d. $\text{Unif}(0,1)$ weights. Let $T_n$ be the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of $G_n$. The expected weight of $T_n$ is known to converge to $ζ(3) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{k^3}$ (Frieze 1985). We investigate the sum of weights of edges incident to the leaves of $T_n$, denoting this quantity by $L_n$. We give tight upper and lower bounds on $\mathbb{E}[L_n]$ and determine its limit as $n$ diverges, leveraging typical behavior of sparse Erdős--Rényi random graphs. We also establish concentration of $L_n$ around $\mathbb{E}[L_n]$ and almost sure convergence to this value. These results directly yield substantial improvements to state-of-the-art bounds for two important variants of the MST problem: (1) an improved upper bound on the weight of the optimal random instance Steiner tree, as studied by Bollobás, Gamarnik, Riordan, and Sudakov (2004); and (2) an improvement over the upper bound for the Probabilistic Minimum Spanning Tree, introduced by Bertsimas (1988).

papers.title: Exploring Low-Regret Energy System Transition Pathways with Modeling to Generate Alternatives
papers.abstract: Long-term planning of energy system transitions is complex due to interdependent investment decisions and uncertain market and policy conditions. Stochastic optimization models account for this uncertainty by identifying a single optimal hedging strategy. However, the flexibility in technology choice and investment timing, i.e., the transition flexibility, usually remains unexplored. Modeling to generate alternatives (MGA) explores near-optimal solution spaces but has not been coupled with stochastic optimization to quantify the transition flexibility. We explore the low-regret pathway space, i.e., all transition pathways that stay within a chosen regret tolerance in every scenario. We introduce a termination criterion for MGA that bounds the exploration error in high-dimensional solution spaces and measure how far each pathway decision, once taken, narrows the capacity ranges of the others. We apply the method to an industrial energy system in Germany. The pathway that minimizes the worst-case regret keeps it at 2.2%, compared with up to 30.9% for perfect-foresight pathways. The transition flexibility increases most at low regret tolerances. At 3.5%, the capacity ranges are on average about 60% as wide as at the highest regret tolerance of 10%. A large share of these capacity ranges is surplus capacity, i.e., capacity installed in addition to, not instead of, other capacity. Surplus capacity is largely not operated but, once installed, narrows the other capacity ranges more strongly than operated capacity. Exploring the low-regret pathway space, rather than reporting a single optimal pathway, therefore is the more informative basis for planning energy system transitions under uncertainty.

papers.title: On the Starshapedness of the Symmetrized Bidisc
papers.abstract: It is well known that the symmetrized bidisc $\mathbb{G}_2$ is star-like about the point $(0,0)$. In our attempt to check if there are other points about which $\mathbb{G}_2$ is star-like, we find that $\mathbb{G}_2$ cannot be starlike about any point $(s,p)\neq(0,0)\in \mathbb{G}_2$.

papers.title: Second-Order Cone Valid Inequalities for Set-Point Tracking with Energy Storage
papers.abstract: Convex relaxations of energy storage models drop the complementarity constraints that forbid simultaneous charging and discharging. In the set-point tracking problem, the relaxation can then charge and discharge simultaneously at no cost, as the tracking error depends only on the net power of the storage. We show that the convex hull of the single-period epigraph of the tracking error, under complementarity, is the epigraph of a parabolic cylinder. The resulting second-order cone inequality adds to the tracking error a penalty on the product of the charging and discharging powers and is the tightest convex member of the pencil of quadrics through the two branches of the epigraph. With power limits and the mode variable, the hull is given by the perspective reformulation of the two modes, which dominates the cylinder. In 20000 instances, the cylinder reduces the hours with simultaneous charging and discharging by more than 99% and yields an optimal schedule in 98.8% of them.

papers.title: Mean curvature flow into an ambient Riemannian manifold evolving by Ricci-Bourguignon flow
papers.abstract: We study the mean curvature flow in Riemannian manifolds evolving by the Ricci-Bourguignon flow. Using DeTurck's trick, we establish short-time existence and uniqueness for the mean curvature flow in this time-dependent ambient geometry. In the case where the ambient metric evolves by a self-similar solution to the Ricci-Bourguignon flow, we characterize the associated mean curvature solitons and derive a Huisken monotonicity-type formula adapted to the Ricci-Bourguignon setting. As a consequence, we show that, in compact ambient manifolds, type-I singularities of the mean curvature flow in a gradient shrinking Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background have, after suitable parabolic rescaling, weighted minimal hypersurfaces as their limiting models, while in the noncompact setting, we establish the corresponding result for a gradient shrinking Schouten soliton background. This provides a geometric framework for understanding how the ambient scalar curvature influences the formation and structure of singularity models for the mean curvature flow. We also show how to construct explicit examples of mean curvature flow in a gradient Ricci-Bourguignon soliton background.

papers.title: On $U(1)^{2}$-Invariant Cayley $4$-Folds in $\mathbb{R}^{8}$
papers.abstract: We study $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley submanifolds in $ \mathbb{R}^{8} $, under the action with weights $ (e^{i θ_{1}}, e^{i θ_{2}}, e^{-i(θ_{1} + θ_{2})}, 1) $ on coordinates $ (z_{1}, z_{2}, z_{3}, z_{4}) \in \mathbb{C}^{4} $. Locally, we can prove that $ N $ can be written as a graph of functions $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2}: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ (where $ a_{3}= -a_{1}-a_{2} $), where unlike in the special Lagrangian setting, the moment-map parameters are not required to be constant, which gives rise to additional degrees of freedom in the reduced equations. We prove that $ N $ is Cayley if and only if a non-linear, Cauchy-Riemann system of partial differential equations in $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2} $ holds, with ellipticity away from its degeneracy locus. We investigate the special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions of the system, obtaining potential functions in both cases. For general $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley $ 4 $-folds, we derive almost-conservation laws (with clear obstruction terms) involving natural $ S_{3} $-invariant and alternating combinations of the moment-map parameters. These identities exhibit additional source terms, distinguishing the general Cayley system from its special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions.

papers.title: Crossing Numbers of Complete Graphs: the independent odd crossing number
papers.abstract: We show that the Harary--Hill bound on the crossing number of complete graphs as well as the Zarankiewwicz bound on the crossing number of complete bipartite graphs, both recently established by OpenAI, also hold for the independent odd crossing number. This implies that the same bounds hold for several other crossing number variants such as the (independent) algebraic crossing number and the (independent) pair crossing number.

papers.title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

papers.title: Almost Controlled: The FDR of Benjamini-Hochberg on Weighted Conformal p-Values
papers.abstract: Weighted conformal p-values generalize conformal inference to cases with covariate shift. One way to use them is to pass them to the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure, either to decide which test units to select or to detect outliers. But weighted conformal p-values may not be positively dependent, so we want to know: does BH still control the false discovery rate (FDR) in finite samples? Based on experiments, it appears to, but we prove it doesn't. We give two counterexamples, certified in exact rational arithmetic, where the FDR exceeds its target level $q$. We also identify how large the difference between the FDR and $q$ can be. With $n$ calibration points, $m$ test units and weight ratio $B$, the relative excess $\mathrm{FDR}/q-1$ is bounded by a function of $n$, $m$, $B$ and $q$ that is of order $\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ when $Bm/(nq)$ is small. The bound holds for every configuration with $B\le n$ and every $n$. This order can be reached when multiple non-null test units share a common threshold: in a Poisson-limit model, that configuration's excess is $c(q)\sqrt{Bm/(nq)}$ to first order as $B/n\to0$ and then $m\to\infty$. For some fixed distributions with this structure, the excess decreases only like $n^{-1/2}$ as $n$ grows. If every test unit is null, the excess is $O(B/n)$ at fixed $m$, and in certain configurations it grows linearly with $m$. To assist practitioners in judging how large the FDR can be, we turn that bound, which depends only on $n$, $m$, $q$ and $B$, into a lowered BH level with proved finite-sample control, and give a much less conservative rule of thumb that covers every worst case we were able to find but provides no guarantee.

papers.title: Melnikov residuals and stationary amalgamation in PAC fields
papers.abstract: We construct an invariant symmetric ternary relation with existence and stationarity over models for classes of characteristic-zero Frobenius fields associated with Melnikov formations. For proper formations, the automorphism theories of their canonical root-predicate expansions have amalgamation and no model companion. The underlying fields are then unbounded, and their theories are NSOP$_1$ but not simple. In this case, on triples of elementary submodels, the constructed relation implies ordinary nonforking, which implies Kim-independence, which implies linear disjointness; all three implications are strict. We also study p.e.c. fields with group actions, namely fields existentially closed in every regular extension carrying an extension of the action. We prove that the class of p.e.c.\ difference fields of characteristic zero is not elementary, and that the theory of all characteristic-zero difference fields with canonical root predicates has no model companion.

papers.title: Generic splitting types and Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most eighteen lines in the complex projective plane is determined by the intersection lattice. In particular, Terao's freeness conjecture holds for seventeen and eighteen lines. For any number of lines, it holds for free arrangements whose smaller exponent is at most eight. By the theorem for at most sixteen lines, the problem reduces to a uniformity condition for lattices of seventeen lines: if all realizations have minimal Jacobian-syzygy degree at least seven, then all or none have degree seven. The proof has two parts. First, a realization of minimal degree seven has defect at most four, the defect being the length of the zero scheme of a minimal section. This uses the residual inflection quartic of the associated degree-seven foliation, local inflection identities, and fixed-point theory for critically fixed rational maps of degree seven with exact finite certificates. Second, the uniformity condition holds at these defects. For multiplicities at most six, a critical realization contains a twelve-line core of minimal weight, and an exact search through extensions of the cores shows that the lattice has a single Galois orbit of realizations; the only family left at defect four has no critical member. For a point of multiplicity seven we use the zero scheme of the pencil derivation and a classification of transversal structures. Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines needs only defects one, two and three and, for seventeen lines, this classification at multiplicity seven. The proof is computer-assisted.

papers.title: Singular sets of conformal curves are discrete
papers.abstract: We prove that the differential of a non-constant conformal curve between Euclidean spaces has full rank outside a discrete set. In particular, conformal curves are real-analytic outside a discrete set. We provide examples of entire associative and coassociative conformal curves with a non-empty singular set. We show that every non-constant Special Lagrangian conformal curve is a real-analytic conformal immersion. We also prove that a non-constant conformal curve has discrete fibers.

papers.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
papers.abstract: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. The recently introduced Quantum Oracle Sketching builds quantum oracles from random data streams without storing them. We combine coherent loading of separately reported sub-bits, exact in reliable rounds and by Quantum Oracle Sketching in continuous broadcast, with nonlinear fusion and Hidden Matching readout. The register count $R$ does not grow with $N$, and the memory is $O(\log N)$ logical qubits and classical bits, at fixed $b$, graph bounds, thresholds and error targets: an exponential memory advantage over every classical receiver and over Hidden Matching with that buffer. We prove unbiasedness in reliable rounds, preparation bounds in continuous broadcast, classical lower bounds and, for a planner-supplied multi-hop coefficient stream, spectral error bounds. Broadcast simulations match analytic averages at $N=1024$, without resolved bias growth up to $N=2^{20}$. Fault-tolerant hardware, gate rates and, in continuous broadcast, report counts remain open.

papers.title: Cantor Julia sets of positive area in non-autonomous dynamics
papers.abstract: For every $a>0$, we prove the existence of a sequence of polynomials with rational coefficients whose non-autonomous iteration produces a Julia set of planar area $a$. We also construct a sequence of rational maps with rational coefficients whose Julia set has the same prescribed area. No individual map in this rational sequence is Möbius-conjugate to a polynomial, and no choice of Möbius coordinates at successive phases turns it into a polynomial sequence. In both cases, for every $n\geq1$, the Julia set obtained by starting the iteration at the $n$-th map, called the phase-$n$ Julia set, is a Cantor set and meets every neighborhood of each of its points in positive planar area. For every $A\in(0,1)$, we construct two sequences of quadratic polynomials, each with $\infty$ in every phase Julia set and with first phase Julia set of normalized spherical area $A$. In one sequence, every phase Julia set is a Cantor set of locally positive spherical area. In the other, every phase Julia set has countably infinitely many connected components and equals the closure of its interior. Both sequences admit invariant measurable line fields whose essential supports are the corresponding phase Julia sets. Finally, for every $d\in[0,2]$, we construct a sequence of quadratic polynomials for which every phase Julia set is a Cantor set of zero spherical area with local Hausdorff dimension $d$ at each of its points.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.title: Expansion in powers of simple groups of Lie type
papers.abstract: We prove an expansion theorem for direct powers of all nonabelian finite simple groups $G$ other than the alternating groups and the Suzuki groups ${}^2B_2(q)$. If $G^m$ is generated by $d\ge2$ elements, then $G^m$ has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements and normalized spectral gap at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C>0$. In particular, this answers a question of Sabatini on $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)^p$. For $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, we use the expander graphs constructed by Lubotzky--Samuels--Vishne, and an amplification trick for direct powers; in high rank, we use the Ershov--Jaikin-Zapirain property (T) theorem.

papers.title: Ice and mirrors
papers.abstract: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable. We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Quantum Networks with Realistic Photonic Memories
papers.abstract: Ensemble based photonic memories paired with photon pair sources are the essential ingredient for many quantum networking protocols. Most protocols and theoretical analyses focus on networks of identical nodes, however, realistic networks consist of nodes that may vary from device to device. We investigate a network of non-identical memories and develop mitigation strategies for the variation in performance. We find that by strategically distributing the memories among the nodes and individually adapting the emission probabilities based on the memory efficiency the effect of the variance on fidelity and duration can to a large extend be mitigated. Generally, our analysis shows the importance of accounting and compensating for device variations to avoid deteriorating the performance. Lastly, we also link our results to memories where efficiency decays as a function of storage duration. Here, we show that our approach provides a visible improvement for networks with non-identical and decaying memories.

papers.title: Sharp High-Dimensional Gaussian Approximations over Rectangles without Covariance Restrictions
papers.abstract: We study how well a sum of $n$ independent random vectors with $p$ coordinates can be approximated by a Gaussian vector with the same mean and covariance. We measure the error over rectangles, so the bounds apply to maxima and simultaneous confidence regions. The coordinates may be arbitrarily dependent, even exactly linearly dependent, and the bounds do not deteriorate as the covariance matrix becomes singular. After standardizing the coordinate variances, bounded or sub-exponential coordinates give the $n^{-1/2}$ sample-size rate up to logarithmic factors, with the size or tail bounds held fixed. The main upper bounds retain the Gaussian expected maximum, improving the rates when the coordinates are strongly dependent. Fourth-moment refinements give further improvements when large observations contribute little to individual coordinate variances. If we instead impose a fixed moment bound of order $q>4$ on the largest absolute coordinate, together with a coordinate fourth-moment bound, the rate becomes $n^{-1/2+1/q}$ up to logarithmic factors. At $q=4$, the slower $n^{-1/4}$ rate is unavoidable, confirming our earlier conjecture. We also allow the bounds on observation size to grow with $n$. Lower-bound examples show that the dependence on sample size, observation size, and Gaussian width is sharp up to logarithmic factors in the regimes studied, and in several regimes the upper and lower bounds match including the logarithmic terms.

papers.title: A proof of the Reinhardt conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Reinhardt conjecture: among centrally symmetric convex disks in the plane, the smoothed regular octagon has the least optimal lattice packing density, and equality holds precisely for its nonsingular affine images. The proof combines explicit bounds on the number of control arcs, local cost inequalities and rigorous finite verification of the remaining switching types.

papers.title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
papers.abstract: Physics-informed operator learning trains neural operators on the residual of a parametric partial differential equation (PDE) instead of labeled solution data, but its reliability depends on a variationally correct residual: one that is equivalent to the error in a norm dictated by the equation, the PDE-compliant norm. For nonlinear equations written as first-order systems, we prove that the first-order system least-squares residual is equivalent to the error in this norm near a solution branch if the linearized residual is stable and the residual derivative is Lipschitz continuous, possibly in a norm stronger than the error norm. We verify these conditions for monotone reaction, solution- and gradient-dependent diffusion, and compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity. The stability mechanisms vary across these classes, as do the regions where the equivalence holds, from arbitrary bounded sets to a neighborhood of the branch. In a conforming finite element space, we show that the loss excess of a state near the finite element solution is equivalent to its squared distance from that solution. We use this loss to train a reduced basis neural operator with values in this space, with solution snapshots needed only for the basis and the loss and its symbolically derived gradient assembled by the finite element library. At inference, this loss estimates the error. Numerically, the square root of the loss excess tracks the error within factors comparable to those of the linear case, and the operator achieves higher accuracy in the PDE-compliant norm than grid-based baselines evaluated in the same finite element space.

papers.title: Multi-bubble blowup for the energy supercritical Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: This article establishes the existence of finite time multi-bubble Type II blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Given integers $K\geq 2$ and $L\geq 2$, a positive integer exponent $p$, and a dimension $d>d_\ast(p,K,L)$, we construct solutions concentrating at any prescribed $K$ distinct points $\{x_j\}_{j=1}^K\subset\mathbb R^d$, with the asymptotic form \begin{equation*} ψ(t,x)=λ^{\frac1p}(t)\sum_{j=1}^K Q\big(λ(t)(x-x_j)\big)+ζ^\ast(x)+o_{\dot H^σ}(1),\qquad t\to0, \end{equation*} where $λ(t)=t^{-\frac12-ν}$, $ν=-\frac12-\frac{L}{λ_+}$, $s_c=\frac d2-\frac1p$, and $s_c<σ<s_c+\frac{4ν}{1+2ν}$. Here $Q$ is the positive radial stationary profile, $λ_+$ is the slow characteristic exponent in its asymptotic expansion at infinity and $ζ^\ast$ is the limiting radiation determined by the outer profile. The proof combines a matched asymptotic construction of a finite order approximate solution with high order energy estimates and a compactness argument. The key ingredients are the elimination of the self-similar oscillatory branch through a quantized choice of blowup rate and the quantitative control of the combined algebraic tails of the translated ground state potentials.

papers.title: Regularity of Gaussian processes, metric entropy and the Wills functional
papers.abstract: We establish exact relations between three quantities: the growth of the Gaussian Wills functional under dilations, the small-scale metric entropy of the index set, and the critical Hölder exponent of the associated isonormal Gaussian process. For every compact Gaussian-bounded set $T$, the Wills growth exponent $ρ(T)$, the entropy exponent $η(T)$, and the critical Hölder exponent $α_H(T)$ satisfy \[ η(T)=\frac{2ρ(T)}{2-ρ(T)}, \qquad α_H(T) =1-\frac{η(T)}{2} =\frac{2-2ρ(T)}{2-ρ(T)}. \] Thus any one of these parameters determines the other two. Our main tools are a Wills-functional analogue of Sudakov's minoration and a complementary upper bound for $W(rT)$ in terms of local Gaussian widths.

papers.title: Computing with Orientation-Dependent Vector Fields in Crystallographic Texture Analysis
papers.abstract: We present a computational framework for representing orientation-dependent vector fields. Building on (arXiv:2608.21235), we translate the differential-geometric formulation into crystallographic notation and focus on its computational use in crystallographic texture analysis. In crystallographic applications, small orientation changes are commonly described by rotation vectors, spin tensors, or infinitesimal misorientations. By contrast, vector fields in harmonic computations are usually represented by components with respect to Euler-angle derivatives, following the classical formulation of generalized spherical harmonics. This representation is convenient but numerically unfavorable. We instead use rotation-vector components, extending a familiar description of individual orientation changes to orientation-dependent vector fields. In this representation, vector fields are described by three scalar component functions, which can be expanded into generalized spherical harmonics. We derive frequency-domain formulas for gradient, divergence, and curl, enabling their evaluation directly on harmonic coefficients. In particular, the gradient of a band-limited scalar function remains band-limited with the same bandwidth.

papers.title: Counting Matrices of Prescribed Jordan Type in Incidence Algebras
papers.abstract: We count nilpotent matrices in the incidence algebra of a finite poset over a finite field that belong to a prescribed conjugacy class for the adjoint action of the general linear group. We prove that these counts depend only on the comparability graph of the poset. We introduce shuffle-prefix posets, a class containing all finite interval orders, and give explicit formulas for their nilpotent Jordan counts. These counts are polynomials with integer coefficients in the field size, valid over every finite field. Finally, Fourier duality relates conjugacy-class counts in a coordinate subspace to those in the subspace supported on the complementary matrix positions, whenever one subspace consists entirely of nilpotent matrices.

papers.title: Experimental simulation of a Hilbert-space inner-product change
papers.abstract: We simulate an effective change in a single qubit's inner product (IP) by implementing the channel $\mathcal{F}^η$ on a superconducting quantum processor. Whereas previous experiments simulated parity-time (PT)-symmetric dynamics with a fixed IP, this experiment implements the IP-change channel itself for metrics associated with PT-symmetric systems. Building on an earlier adversarial verification approach, we derive a process-fidelity threshold that rules out mixtures of qubit unitary operations with random discarding of runs. We test the channel for 40 metrics using a single qutrit and a two-qubit Stinespring dilation. The measured fidelities exceed the threshold in 24 of 40 qutrit instances after readout error mitigation, compared with 16 of 40 unmitigated two-qubit instances. Without mitigation, 14 of 40 qutrit instances pass. These results demonstrate a direct simulation of an effective Hilbert-space IP change and its verification against a specified adversarial class, while showing the importance of readout treatment in comparing the encodings.

papers.title: Plenitude of ideal correlations explains quantum theory
