papers.abstract: We show that the Hilbert-space formalism and the Born rule of quantum theory are singled out by the following principle: every correlation that is possible in a theory in which every observable admits an ideal measurement is physically realizable. An ideal measurement is one that yields the same outcome when repeated and does not disturb any compatible observable.

papers.title: On elliptic curves with prescribed analytic rank at least $2$
papers.abstract: Zywina recently showed that infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ have rank $2$, settling a long-standing open question. We explore the analytic version of this problem, showing that every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ has infinitely many quadratic twists with analytic rank either $2$ or $4$, subject to GRH. We also obtain, under the same assumption, infinitely many congruent number curves with odd analytic rank between $3$ and $17$.

papers.title: Bernstein-type inequalities for Markov processes via resolvent estimates
papers.abstract: We establish Bernstein-type inequalities for additive functionals of Markov processes through uniform resolvent estimates between a Banach space and its dual. Under an iterated Poincaré inequality, we obtain the classical Bernstein form sought by Huang and Li in [5], up to numerical constants, in both continuous and discrete time. Suitable choices of the Banach space recover Bernstein-type bounds under Poincaré and Sobolev inequalities and allow unbounded observables. For normal generators, a criterion involving the modulus of the generator captures the contribution of its antisymmetric part. As an application, we obtain Bernstein-type inequalities for $L^{3/2}$ observables of a non-mixing diffusion on the two-dimensional torus. The proof combines perturbation estimates for the Feynman--Kac resolvent with the stationary increment property of additive functionals of stationary processes.

papers.title: Numerical approximation of Benjamin-Ono type models for two-dimensional internal waves
papers.abstract: In this paper we analyze the numerical approximation with spectral methods of two asymptotic models for the two-dimensional propagation of internal waves in a two-layer system of fluids with rigid-lid condition. The semidiscretization in space of the periodic initial-value problem with the spectral Fourier-Galerkin method is introduced and some error estimates are derived. Then the semidiscrete system is integrated in time with the Implicit Midpoint Rule and several numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the corresponding full discretization.

papers.title: P = W conjectures for varieties with nilpotent fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove the cohomological and the geometric $P=W$ conjectures for the moduli spaces of $G$-Higgs bundles and $G$-local systems on any smooth complex projective variety $X$ with nilpotent fundamental group, and any connected complex reductive group $G$. To the best of our knowledge, our results provide the first instances of $P=W$ conjectures beyond curves and abelian varieties. Finally, we provide examples of our theorem for classical groups: as a byproduct of this analysis we investigate when symplectic resolutions of the corresponding character varieties exist.

papers.title: Perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2)
papers.abstract: We enumerate the parameter matrices of all perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2), n >= 5. We show that there are only five matrices that can be the parameter matrix of such a coloring. Two of them occur if and only if 5 | n, two occur if and only if 3 | n, and the remaining one occurs if and only if 10 | n.

papers.title: Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits
papers.abstract: Weight-space programming removes the thinking loops of a small reasoning model by a rank-one edit W' = W + u v^T of an MLP output matrix, where u is a loop direction and v is the solution of a sparse Linear Program (LP) over the neuron activations. We investigate whether the LP is needed. We replace it by a sort: we take the 8 neurons whose activation has the smallest coefficient of variation, and give them equal shares of the push that the LP solution realizes. On Qwen3.5-0.8B the sorted edit scores 67.0% on 1000 problems (MATH-500 and GSM8K) against 67.4% for the LP edit and 9.5% for the unedited model; the paired difference is -0.4 points, with 95% confidence interval [-2.9, +2.1], inside a non-inferiority margin of 5 points declared before the runs. On three further sampling seeds the difference is -0.6 points, interval [-2.0, +0.8], and -0.8 points, interval [-2.3, +0.6], when the dose is set without the LP. The sort does not solve the LP, but the neurons it shares with the LP solution carry most of its mean push. The outcome is that, on this model, the edit acts as a nearly constant bias along u.

papers.title: On the toric Bando--Kasue--Nakajima conjecture
papers.abstract: The conjecture of Bando, Kasue, and Nakajima asserts that every simply connected Ricci-flat $4$-manifold that is asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE), that is, asymptotic at infinity to a flat cone $\mathbb{R}^4/Γ$, is hyperkähler for one of its orientations. A toric ALE instanton is a Ricci-flat ALE $4$-manifold with an effective isometric action of the $2$-torus; such a manifold is simply connected. We prove the conjecture for the toric ALE instantons whose group at infinity $Γ$ is conjugate in $\mathrm O(4)$ to a subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$: each of them is a multi-Eguchi--Hanson metric with collinear centres. In particular, the conjecture holds for toric ALE instantons with $|Γ|\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$. The proof uses a closed formula for toric gravitational instantons, which expresses the metric through Hankel determinants of a positive measure on the fixed points of the torus action. With it, the problem becomes a question about lattice points in a parallelogram determined by the end.

papers.title: Bregman primal-dual methods for conic linear optimization via exact-penalty and self-dual formulations
papers.abstract: We study Bregman primal--dual proximal methods for conic linear programs (LPs). For problems involving non-polyhedral cones, Bregman distances lead to generalized projections that are often simpler than Euclidean projections. In this paper, we reformulate conic LPs as equivalent exact-penalty problems over truncated cones, and use self-dual embeddings to construct such formulations systematically. This approach yields Bregman proximal methods with simpler subproblems and convergence guarantees over bounded domains. We also study line searches for the Bregman primal--dual hybrid gradient and extragradient methods applied to self-dual problems. For logarithmically homogeneous kernels, the Bregman distances from the starting points are unbounded on the truncated cone, and the classical ergodic bounds do not apply. For these kernels, we derive convergence rates for the exact-penalty objective at the averaged iterates of both methods. Numerical experiments with nonnegative trigonometric polynomial optimization and sparse semidefinite optimization indicate the potential of this framework as a general-purpose approach for incorporating efficient Bregman projections in conic linear optimization.

papers.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
papers.abstract: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities. The classical phase space acquires a metric of its own when a vacuum is chosen: quantizing a linear system amounts to choosing a compatible complex structure, equivalently a compatible metric $g$. We take this second metric as the primary object and show that it plays, on phase space, the role that the quantum metric plays on the space of states: fluctuations of linear observables are $g$-norms of Hamiltonian vector fields, and along coherent states $g/2\hbar$ \emph{is} the quantum metric. Squeezed states then have a simple description. A squeezed vacuum is the vacuum of another metric, and squeezing is a property of a pair of metrics, a relative vacuum, whose invariants are the eigenvalues $e^{\pm2r_i}$ of $L=g_0^{-1}g$. We work out the harmonic oscillator in detail, including why a rotated squeezed state no longer minimizes the product of the displayed uncertainties. Quadratic evolution deforms the metric, and only the part of the generator that is self-adjoint with respect to the reference changes the $r_i$, at a rate we give exactly. For fields, a vacuum is unitarily implementable relative to a reference exactly when it lies at finite distance from it in the space of vacua. For a massless field in de Sitter space we revisit the two canonical charts compared by Grain and Vennin: relative to the reference of the standard squeezing formalism the Bunch--Davies state has $\sinh r_k=1/(2|kη|)$, and relative to the vacuum that a radiation era beginning at time $η$ would select it has $\sinh r_k=1/(2k^2η^2)$. The second comparison squeezes twice as fast and is unitarily implementable; the first is not.

papers.title: Siphon faces in slow-fast mass-action networks
papers.abstract: When the species of a siphon in a mass-action network, however many, are fast and their invariant face loses transverse stability along the slow flow, trajectories follow the face past this loss before leaving it. We study three consequences. (i) If the transverse Metzler linearisation is irreducible, the entry-exit relation with its Perron root gives the exit. Under acyclic feeding between its strongly connected components, a max-plus recursion over the reactions gives it; in general neither the Perron root nor the diagonal blocks do. (ii) With one slow species, acyclic feeding and a transversal exit, a fold of the interior critical manifold followed by a drop onto the face gives a unique, exponentially attracting relaxation oscillation whose turning points tend to the fold and exit point. Exactly $3474$ minimal planar networks of molecularity $\leq 3$, with fast per-capita rate affine and decreasing in the slow species, meet our sufficient conditions for it. (iii) A siphon-breaking reaction of rate $δ$ and finite min-plus breaking order $w$ unfolds the transcritical point into a fold if a Perron-weighted second-order self-interaction is positive, and not if negative; the fold's critical component lies at distance of order $δ^{w/2}$ from the face. For $δ=e^{-μ/^Karepsilon}$ the broken face is a floor at $-μ$ in the recursion, and planar cycles leave it between the entry-exit and transcritical points, depending on $μ$. Simulations confirm predicted exits and cycles, including cyclic feeding, where the prediction is conjectural, and high-precision computations confirm the folds; the errors shrink as $^Karepsilon$ or $δ$ decreases.

papers.title: Sumsets modulo ideals: Baire category and descriptive complexity
papers.abstract: Given an ideal $\mathcal I$ on the nonnegative integers, we study the family $Σ(\mathcal I)$ of all sets for which every $\mathcal{I}$-small modification is not a nontrivial sumset $A+B$. We prove that $Σ(\mathcal I)$ is comeager whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an Erdős--Ulam ideal generated by a nonincreasing sequence of positive weights. This answers an open question for the ideal $\mathcal{Z}$ of asymptotic density zero sets in [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{151} (2023), 3681--3689]. We also show that $Σ(\mathcal I)$ is either empty or a dense $G_δ$-complete set whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an $F_σ$ ideal which is invariant under finite modifications. This implies that the family of nontrivial sumsets $A+B$ is $F_σ$-complete (hence, Borel). On the other hand, we construct a meager ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $Σ(\mathcal I)$ is neither meager nor comeager. Finally, we prove that $Σ(\mathcal Z)$ is coanalytic and not $F_{σδ}$.

papers.title: Rethinking Entropic Uncertainty: How measuring without a trace leads to longer keys
papers.abstract: In recent years, the entropic uncertainty relation (EUR) has been one of the most prominent tools to obtain tight key rates secure against general coherent attacks for a broad class of quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. Despite its success, the fundamental question of how to incorporate the statistics of more than two mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) directly into the EUR is yet to be answered. Here, we introduce a simple yet powerful shift of perspective: Instead of the usual tripartition into the systems of Alice, Bob and Eve, we treat Alice and Bob as one joint system and introduce an additional register as the third system. This register contains the results of appropriately chosen virtual measurements that leave no trace in the real branch of the protocol, but act as a conditioning on the counterfactual phase error measurements. We show that this allows us to obtain tight key rates for QKD protocols using an arbitrary number of MUBs directly and natively from the EUR. Moreover, we demonstrate that this approach has a much broader relevance beyond the inclusion of multiple MUBs, allowing for improvements in many existing security proofs and the treatment of previously unexplored aspects for a wide range of protocols.

papers.title: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. This was recently resolved by Sadhu and, independently, by Pach, Tardos, and Zeng, based on a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich. These papers showed that $k$-quasiplanar graphs have at most $k^{O(k)}n$ edges. In this note, we greatly improve the dependence on $k$ and show that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. The proof is based on a geometric charging scheme and Erdős-Szekeres type combinatorial arguments.

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(π/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\fracπ{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $π/2$ and $π/4$, respectively.

papers.title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
papers.abstract: Modeling large multi-agent systems poses challenges for trajectory inference and parameter identification, as network size and coupling increase computational demands and partial observations require reconstructing unobserved states. We propose MAS-PINN, a neural-network architecture with a tailored training algorithm for a physics-informed learning framework that leverages the network topology and the agents' similarity to reduce computational and memory costs of simulating and identifying multi-agent systems. Its architecture represents agent trajectories through shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients. Training alternates between learning features, fitting coupled trajectories, and estimating physical parameters. A matrix-free update exploits local interactions to fit trajectories without forming large global matrices. Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka--Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators show improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, including inference in large systems and identification under partial observations or unknown topology, alongside substantial computational savings in coefficient fitting.

papers.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from $-155\;$dBm to $-130\;$dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from $-95\;$dBm to $-55\;$dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of $6.0\;$GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of $(74.7\pm 0.2) \;$dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of $(75.4\pm 6.8) \;$dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.

papers.title: The Sample Complexity of Channel Coding
papers.abstract: We introduce a new framework for the study and evaluation of the fundamental limits of channel coding, emphasizing genuinely nonasymptotic results. The {\em channel coding sample complexity} $n^*({\cal W},ε)$ of a channel ${\cal W}$ is defined as the smallest blocklength at which it is possible to transmit information through that channel with error probability below $ε$ and at a rate at least as high as that given by an appropriate constraint also in terms of $ε$. This formulation follows analogous developments in statistics, computer science and, more recently, in lossless source coding. For any discrete memoryless channel we derive nonasymptotic bounds on the sample complexity, with explicit constants. These bounds show that the sample complexity is characterized not by the usual channel capacity, but by the channel's Augustin--Csiszár capacity of order $1/2$, which coincides with the cutoff rate as well as with the channel's Sibson capacity of order $1/2$. The proof is partly based on a new channel-coding one-shot converse in terms of hypothesis testing. We also examine extensions of the sample complexity framework to general target rates. Moreover, we derive corresponding results for the sample complexity of the additive white Gaussian noise channel with a quadratic power constraint. Their proof relies on new, explicit upper bounds on the best achievable error probability, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Nonparametric Instrumental Kernel Regression: The Well- and Misspecified Setting Under General Link Conditions
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric instrumental variable regression when the outcome takes values in a separable Hilbert space $\mathbb{Y}$, for instance a curve, a density or the kernel mean embedding of a distribution. The structural function solves an ill-posed operator equation whose conditional expectation operator need not be injective, and whose solutions need not belong to the hypothesis space. We analyse a two-stage kernel estimator that extends kernel instrumental variable regression to $\mathbb{Y}$-valued outcomes and allows spectral regularisation in both stages, including Landweber iteration and Showalter's method in the second stage. We show that the second stage is a regularisation method in the Hilbert scale generated by the inverse of the kernel integral operator. This viewpoint identifies the solution towards which the estimator converges: the minimum-norm solution in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space in the well-specified case and, in the misspecified case, the unique solution in the range of the continuous extension of the projection operator associated to the well-specified setting. Under source conditions and link conditions expressed through general index functions, we derive non-asymptotic bounds in a scale of interpolation norms that hold with high probability in terms of the first-stage error, with or without identification and in the well- and misspecified settings. For polynomial link conditions, we recover the rate of scalar kernel instrumental regression and extend it to targets outside the hypothesis space; for exponential link conditions, we obtain logarithmic rates in the severely ill-posed regime.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: Vanishing Relative Distance of Uniformly Random CSS LDPC Codes Built from Permutation Matrices
papers.abstract: Classical random regular low-density parity-check codes can have minimum distance growing linearly with block length. We study CSS check matrices formed as full $J\times L$ arrays of arbitrary $P\times P$ permutation matrices, sampled uniformly subject to commutation. For fixed column weight $J\ge3$ and fixed even row weight $L>2J$, we prove that the relative minimum distance converges to zero in probability as $P\to\infty$, with block length $n=LP$. We analyze the weight enumerators that count all nontrivial logical representatives after excluding stabilizers. A coefficientwise lower bound shows that, at every fixed relative weight $0<α<1$ along even-weight sequences, exponentially many such representatives exist with high probability. Their typical and mean counts have exponent lower bound $h_2(α)/2$, where $h_2$ is the binary entropy function. We compare this bound with the classical LDPC and dense CSS mean weight-distribution exponents. The existence, with high probability, of a logical operator below every fixed target weight $δn$ yields the distance conclusion.

papers.title: \(A_α\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_α(G)=αD(G)+(1-α)A(G)\) for \(0\leqα<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_α\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_α(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters. These sets contain no rational parameters other than \(0\) and \(1/2\), for which the adjacency and signless Laplacian cases are characterized by gcd criteria. For even-order paths rooted at either central vertex, we explicitly evaluate the root resultant and the walk-determinant polynomial in the rooted-product factorization. The resulting controllability criterion combines \(A_α\)-controllability of the base graph with at most three explicit spectral exclusions. For each parameter, one of two fixed complementary base graphs yields controllable products for every even-order path and both central roots. For \(1/2\leqα<1\), algebraic conjugates further simplify the spectral test for general rooted products.

papers.title: Douglas--Rachford Algorithm with Relaxed Resolvents
papers.abstract: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm is a classical method for finding a zero of the sum of two maximally monotone operators. In its standard form, both operators are reflected in the same manner and are activated with the same step-size. In this article we break this symmetry by replacing the reflected resolvents by relaxed resolvents, letting the two operators be activated with different step-sizes. We show that this additional freedom is available precisely when the operators are cocoercive, the admissible range of the parameter being determined by their cocoercivity constants and reducing to the classical algorithm when these constants vanish. Within this range we quantify the averagedness of the resulting operator, which yields the weak convergence of the method together with relaxation steps beyond those allowed in the classical case, and, when one of the operators is in addition strongly monotone, a strict contraction. We compute in closed form the parameters minimizing the contraction factor and we exhibit instances attaining it, so that the resulting linear rates are tight. The optimal rates are strictly smaller than the best rates available for the classical Douglas--Rachford algorithm in the monotone inclusion and convex optimization settings, which are studied separately. All theoretical rates are corroborated by the numerical worst cases obtained via performance estimation.

papers.title: An improved weighted broad $L^2$ estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For a compact smooth plane curve $S$ with nonzero curvature and a union $X\subseteq B_R$ of unit balls satisfying a one-dimensional Katz--Tao condition, we prove $\|\mathrm{Br}_A E_S f\|_{L^2(X)} \leq C_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'} R^{\varepsilon}|X|^{13/62}\|f\|_2$. The proof relies on a refined local broad estimate that uses density decomposition and the short frequency intervals associated with coarse tubes.

papers.title: Information Causality Defeats Every Finite NPA Level
papers.abstract: For every finite level of the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy, we construct correlations that satisfy all its constraints but violate information causality. At each fixed level, one use of a binary-outcome correlation and one classical bit suffice for a violation that grows without bound as the number of measurement settings increases. Information causality bounds the information gained about independent database bits, summed over possible requests, by the length of the message. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound; the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of settings. The violation remains unbounded even when all outcome probabilities are positive and, for any fixed number of measurement settings on each side, every choice of those settings admits a local model. One communicated bit therefore exposes an unbounded gap between information causality and every finite NPA level.

papers.title: Sequential strategy for depolarizing strength estimation
papers.abstract: We study the advantages of applying a sequential strategy for enhancing the precision in estimating the strength $p$ of a depolarizing channel, using qudit and two-qubit probes. The sequential strategy requires that the same depolarizing channel is repeatedly applied $M$ times to the quantum probe. From the analysis of the probe's output state, both the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and its regularization RQFI, given from multiplication by $p$, are analyzed. We determine that in the limit of $p \to 0$, the QFI is {\it linearly amplified} with the number of channel repetitions. Instead, in the weak-noise regime, the QFI is maximized at a finite value of $M$. Then, the RQFI decreases more quickly with $p$ as $M$ increases. In particular, for two-qubit probes, the RQFI decreases with the depolarization strength proportionally to the amount of correlation between the qubits. The greater the number of channel repetitions, the wider the range of $p$ for which the initial state of the probe that allows for the maximization of the QFI is a separable state. We also show that a single qubit probe undergoing a sequential encoding protocol outperforms the optimal two-qubit single-round QFI for $M>3$ in the weak-noise regime.

papers.title: On the blow-up of the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two
papers.abstract: We establish three-term asymptotics for the one-particle Lieb-Thirring constant in dimension two as $γ\to 0$ and identify, up to rescaling and symmetries, the profile of the asymptotically worst potential. The proof uses the well-known relation between the one-particle constant and an integral moment of optimizers of the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Through the optimizers' characterization as positive, vanishing solutions of the nonlinear elliptic equation $-ΔQ + Q = Q^{s}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, the essence of the proof lies in the asymptotic analysis of solutions $Q$ as $s\to\infty$.

papers.title: Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
papers.abstract: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{σ(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{σ(d)}\}$, $σ\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $λ_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_iλ_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $λ_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds. For three, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$ arises, in the optimal dimension $Θ(\log|G|)$, as the residue group of a simplex facet whose $|G|-1$ nonzero box points are Hilbert basis elements of the whole cone; $k$ times such a point is a sum of vertices exactly when its order in $G$ divides $k$. Isolating this arithmetic is costly: if a simplex face has a single Hilbert basis element $h$ that is not a vertex, then $kh$ is a sum of vertices exactly when some $q$ divides $k$, and $d\ge3q-2$, attained for every $q\ge3$; we also find the least dimension for each $G$ with the fewest such elements. Without isolation, every nonzero submonoid of $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ omitting $1$ is $\{k\ge0:kh$ is a sum of vertices$\}$ for a Hilbert basis element $h$ of degree three. For every $0/1$ polytope with $N$ vertices in $\mathbb{R}^r$, three staircase simplices in dimension $O(N(r+1))$ have a face that has IDP exactly when the polytope does. Deciding whether a lattice point $h$ is a sum of vertices is strongly NP-complete, even given vertex expressions of $2h$ and $3h$, and recognizing IDP of a designated facet is coNP-complete; for the whole hull, IDP can first fail in degree linear in $d$, and it holds whenever $d\le5$. For a family of triples defined by words over three letters, we determine the entire Hilbert basis and characterize IDP by two forbidden subsequences.

papers.title: Toeplitz coefficients and the Lu-Tian correspondence on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact embeddable strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold with Reeb field $T$ and Szeg\H o projection $Π$. Herrmann, Hsiao, Marinescu and the second author showed, for any volume form, that the semi-classical cut-offs $χ(k^{-1}ΠPΠ)$ of first-order elliptic self-adjoint Toeplitz operators have full asymptotic expansions. For $P=-\sqrt{-1}T$ and $T$-invariant volume forms, Chang, Herrmann and Hsiao showed that the diagonal coefficients are $a_{j}\intχ(t)t^{n-j}dt$ with local invariants $a_{j}$, computed $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$, and used normal forms in the Sasakian case. We add one step: on a compact Sasakian manifold, regular or not, $a_{j}=a_{j}(g^{T})/(2π^{n+1})$, where $a_{j}(\cdot)$ is the universal Bergman kernel polynomial and $g^{T}$ the transverse Kähler metric; no line bundle on $X$ is needed. This gives an exact correspondence: the logarithmic term of the Szeg\H o kernel vanishes to infinite order over an open set if and only if $a_{j}(g^{T})=0$ there for all $j\ge n+1$, which for circle bundles is a local form of the theorem of Lu and Tian with its converse. For $(n,0)$-forms on complete Sasakian manifolds, a cut-off by the self-adjoint generator of the Reeb flow, which avoids the self-adjointness question for the Toeplitz operator, gives the same results with twisted coefficients.

papers.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

papers.title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
papers.abstract: Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time $τ_m$ leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity. By analyzing a post-Markovian master equation we prove that the Floquet spectrum splits into the ordinary Markovian spectrum plus a replica of the purely unitary Floquet spectrum, uniformly contracted by $e^{-T/τ_m}$, where $T$ is the drive period. Consequently, the DTC signal decay rate becomes independent of any system parameter once $τ_m$ exceeds the Markovian lifetime of the DTC. The measured decay, and in particular its insensitivity to tunable system parameters, thus becomes a direct read-out of the reservoir correlation time. Below this threshold the dynamics is already non-Markovian, but the memory remains hidden in the decay. We confirm this in two structurally unrelated DTCs, a collective long-range model with incoherent pumping and a disorder-free Ising chain with dephasing, where a single estimator recovers $τ_m$. The time crystal thereby witnesses the non-Markovianity of its own environment.

papers.title: Convex polynomial approximation on the unit ball
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{B}^d$ be the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge1$. We prove that, for every convex $f\in C(\mathbb{B}^d)$ and every integer $n\ge1$, there exists a polynomial $P_n$ of total degree at most $n$, convex on all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\|f-P_n\|_{C(\mathbb{B}^d)}\le c\,ω_2(f,n^{-1};\mathbb{B}^d)$. Here $ω_2$ is the ordinary second modulus of smoothness and $c=c_d$ depends only on $d$. In particular, we obtain the rate $O(n^{-2})$ for convex functions with uniformly bounded second derivatives.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: A scaling approach to double phase equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the double phase equation $-Δ_p u - \operatorname{div}(|x|^{-b}\,|\nabla u|^{q-2}\nabla u) = f(|x|,u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, whose operator admits a scaling that acts on both phases simultaneously. Our first main result is a sharp description of the continuous and compact embeddings of the radial energy space into weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^s(\mathbb{R}^N;|x|^{-c})$ with an explicit characterization of their admissible regions in the $(s,c)$-plane. The two critical edges reflect the two phases: on the edge attached to the $p$-phase compactness is lost by spreading to infinity, while on the edge attached to the weighted $q$-phase it is lost by concentration at the origin. Our second main result concerns equations with one critical term on each edge. We show that bounded Palais-Smale sequences either converge or lose at least the energy $β^\ast = \min\{β_1,β_2\}$, where $β_1$ and $β_2$ are the explicit single-phase thresholds, and that this level is optimal when the critical terms are unweighted. Thus, the two mechanisms cannot combine to lower the compactness threshold. Combining these results with a Pohožaev identity, variational methods for scaled functionals and the Fadell-Rabinowitz cohomological index, we prove nonexistence results, obtain an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues on the scaling line and infinitely many solutions for pure power equations, and show that large superscaled and small subscaled perturbations of the doubly critical equation yield multiple solutions.

papers.title: The pinched Veronese has no Koszul filtration
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that the pinched Veronese subalgebra $k [x^3,x^2y,xy^2,x^2z,xz^2,y^3,y^2z,yz^2,z^3] \subset k[x,y,z]$ has no Koszul filtration regardless of the field $k$, despite it being a Koszul algebra. We do this by showing that no ideal $(f,g)$ minimally generated by two linear forms can belong to a Koszul filtration. By the definition of a Koszul filtration this, in turn, implies that no Koszul filtration can exist.

papers.title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
papers.abstract: This paper presents a computational model integrating transmural drug transport, smooth muscle cell contraction, nonlinear anisotropic material behavior, and residual stresses to investigate the effects of calcium channel blockers~(CCBs) on local stress distributions in atherosclerotic arteries. The balance of linear momentum is coupled with a three-dimensional reaction-diffusion equation for the drug transport. Smooth muscle contraction is modeled phenomenologically based on a chemo-mechanical model that incorporates the effects of stretch on intracellular calcium dynamics and calcium sensitization. A novel drug-tissue interaction model is proposed to capture the effects of CCBs on intracellular calcium and thus on smooth muscle contraction. Material parameters are identified by fitting to experimental data from the literature and finite element simulations are conducted on five exemplary atherosclerotic arterial geometries reconstructed from histological cross-sections. Simulation results show that although CCBs reduce the stresses in the media through reduced smooth muscle contraction, they shift load to the fibrous cap, whose stress increases in all five geometries (median of up to 28.9~kPa). This increase varies strongly between plaque morphologies and becomes smaller with lower smooth muscle tone before treatment, lower drug concentrations in the arterial wall and increasing axial pre-stretch. A blood pressure reduction of 10~mmHg already lowers it to a median of at most 3.8~kPa in four of the five geometries. Our findings suggest that CCBs may increase the rupture risk of vulnerable plaques with highly loaded fibrous caps under insufficient blood pressure reduction, which remains to be confirmed experimentally and clinically.

papers.title: Continuous Kakeya type problems with special points that sweep much more area than the rest
papers.abstract: For any $\varepsilon>0$ we construct a continuous motion of a line segment in the plane, such that the center point of the line segment traverses a given bounded set except for a subset of area less than $\varepsilon$, while the rest of the line segment sweeps only an area less than $\varepsilon$. We further show that a circle with a pair of antipodal points removed has the Strong Kakeya Property in the plane: that is, given any two copies of such a punctured circle, we can continuously move one to the other, while staying in a set of arbitrarily small Lebesgue measure. We give a full characterization of those subsets of a great circle that have this property on the sphere. We also show how the first mentioned result can be applied to obtain discontinuity results about the area swept by continuously moving objects.

papers.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
papers.abstract: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.

papers.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-$(1,1)$ maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

papers.title: Stability manifolds and resolutions of singularities
papers.abstract: In this article, we study descent and lifting of Bridgeland stability conditions along Verdier quotients. We give a torsion-pair criterion for lifting every stability condition on the quotient to a weak stability condition with a prescribed heart on the null category. When this criterion holds for every heart on the null category, the space of weak stability conditions with this massless subcategory is homeomorphic to the product of the stability space of the quotient and the discrete set of hearts of bounded $t$-structures on the null category. We apply these results to contractions of relative dimension one, resolutions of nodal varieties, and blowups of smooth projective varieties along smooth centers. For projective surfaces with ADE singularities, we identify the discrete factor through a simply transitive braid group action. When the minimal resolution is a K3 surface, every weak stability condition obtained by lifting a numerical stability condition from the singular surface is the limit of a continuous, quasi-convergent family of numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the resolution with the same heart.

papers.title: Sharp modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for matrix-valued functions on spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that for every smooth positive definite matrix-valued function $g$ on the unit sphere $S^d$, \[ \int_{S^d}\tr(g(\log g-\log\E g))\dd \le\dfrac1{2d}\int_{S^d}\tr((Δg)\log g)\dd. \] Here $μ$ is normalized area measure, $\E g$ is the spherical mean, and $Δ$ is the positive spherical Laplacian. This complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality extends Beckner's sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequality, in its modified form, to matrix-valued functions independent of the matrix size. We show that both entropy and Fisher information decay exponentially under the heat flow with optimal exponent $2d$, whose proof combines the Bochner identity with a $4$th-tensor estimate in the matrix-valued setting.

papers.title: Remarks on Fourier--Mukai invariances
papers.abstract: This note proves that smoothness and Gorensteinness are Fourier--Mukai invariants for proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. Moreover, a kernel realizing such a partnership is perfect if, and only if, the families are smooth.

papers.title: Numerical range of finite perturbations of a 2-periodic weighted shift
papers.abstract: In this note, we consider a weighted shift operator of weight sequence which is a finite perturbation of a 2-periodic weighted shift. We characterise the equality of the closure of its numerical range and its essential numerical range. We end up with some applications and comments.

papers.title: Certified Nash Equilibrium Learning for Nonzero-Sum Jump-Diffusion Games: Policy Iteration and Off-Policy Q-Learning
papers.abstract: This paper establishes two model-free reinforcement learning methods for infinite-horizon N-player linear-quadratic nonzero-sum stochastic differential games whose drift, Brownian diffusion, and Poisson jump amplitudes depend on all players' controls. Control dependence in the diffusion and jump terms couples the players' simultaneous feedback updates. A verifiable certificate ensures that the partially model-free policy iteration map is contractive on an invariant closed ball centered at an admissible initial feedback profile. All feedback iterates are mean-square stabilizing, and the algorithm achieves local geometric convergence of feedback gains and value matrices to those associated with a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. The term certified refers to a verifiable convergence certificate that guarantees mean-square stability of all policy iterates and local geometric convergence to a closed-loop Nash equilibrium. To implement the policy updates from data, the off-policy Q-learning algorithm reuses the same behavior-policy data across iterations without requiring the system coefficients or jump intensity. Under quantitative persistence of excitation and a common initialization, exact population regression reproduces the policy-iteration sequence. The same local convergence guarantee therefore applies to off-policy Q-learning at the population level. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the two proposed algorithms.

papers.title: SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
papers.abstract: Quantum computing requires compilers to translate algorithms represented in the quantum circuit model into unitary operations supported by physical devices. Limited coherence time makes physical execution latency an important compilation objective. Gate fusion can shorten pulses, but gate count and depth do not capture fused targets' control demands. Evaluating every candidate with quantum optimal control (QOC) would embed pulse optimization in structural search. We present Schmidt-guided Compilation for Optimized Pulse Execution (SCOPE), driven by an operator Schmidt time surrogate. The target's angular distance from product operators measures the required nonlocal change; dividing it by a coupling-limited evolution-rate bound gives a lower bound on exact implementation time. Trace-angle and waveform constraints complete block scores for critical-path evaluation during genetic search. Local QOC determines final pulse durations. Under a numerical nearest-neighbor control model, all 104 results across 13 instances from four application families have shorter QOC critical-path durations than an adapted efficient pulse generation framework with advanced synthesis for quantum circuits (EPOC). Using eight-run instance means, the equally weighted reduction is 42.50\%, with a geometric mean speedup of 2.00. In a shared six-qubit quantum Fourier transform (QFT) ablation, time-surrogate guidance reduces mean QOC duration by 22.21\% relative to gate-count guidance and 21.01\% relative to depth guidance, validating the surrogate's joint use in fitness evaluation and mutation-region selection.

papers.title: Singular Global Compactness for Logarithmically Coupled \(p\)-Laplacian Systems
papers.abstract: We establish global compactness for logarithmically coupled p-Laplacian systems on RN, where p=N>4 and bounded positive potentials converge to positive constants at infinity. The finite-energy domain need not be closed under subtraction, obstructing direct profile subtraction. We develop a scalar localisation method using slowly expanding cutoffs and residual commutator estimates uniform in the regularisation parameter. As the regularisation vanishes, residual Palais-Smale sequences split into a solution of the original system and finitely many separating autonomous profiles, with a strongly vanishing remainder and splitting of the logarithmic densities. A converse construction characterises all levels of compactness failure. Applications include convergence of ground-state levels, a compactness-escape alternative for minimising sequences, and a directional response formula for the ground-state energy.

papers.title: In-Context Estimation and Prediction for Parametric ODEs
papers.abstract: Transformers have demonstrated the ability to perform in-context learning, that is, to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without updating their parameters. Existing theory has largely focused on emulating gradient-based algorithms for convex statistical problems or establishing general function approximation guarantees without exploiting the underlying statistical structure. We study in-context parameter estimation and trajectory prediction for parametric ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where estimation is generally nonconvex. Under suitable identifiability and regularity conditions, we construct a transformer that estimates unknown system parameters from noisy trajectory observations through a two-stage approximate maximum likelihood procedure: a coarse search provides an initialization within a locally strongly convex region, followed by gradient descent with local linear contraction. For prediction, we compose this estimator with a neural approximation of the ODE solution map. We further show that, through parameter sharing, a single transformer can perform both parameter estimation and trajectory prediction simultaneously. For these constructions, we establish nonasymptotic guarantees and finite-pretraining oracle inequalities that separate errors due to finite pretraining data, finite context length, and finite-sized transformer approximation. Numerical experiments on linear and nonlinear ODEs further show that pretrained transformers can benefit from longer inference contexts without updating their weights.

papers.title: Quantum-Assisted D-FACTS Scheduling for Moving Target Defense under Switching Limits
papers.abstract: Moving target defense with distributed flexible alternating-current transmission system (D-FACTS) devices re- quires activation decisions as operating points change. Switching limits couple these decisions, but period-by-period rankings can overlook combinations needed to complete low-activation schedules. This paper proposes cross-period candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation to allocate limited physical checks in quantum-assisted D-FACTS scheduling. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) generates activation candidates, while classical scheduling enforces operating and switching constraints. We also quantify model-based activation requirements and test detection through noisy nonlinear trials. A modified IEEE 118-bus study assesses recovery of reference activation and switching objectives within the evaluated set. Combining candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation improves final-budget recovery over period-by-period ranking in the primary operating window for every tested candidate generator. The results show that quantum and classical candidates yield identical recovery curves under combined checking, so the same allocation policy applies to either source.

papers.title: Belavin--Drinfeld bivectors and Poisson deformations
papers.abstract: We study Belavin--Drinfeld Poisson bivectors $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ on $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m}(\mathbb{C})$ from the perspective of Poisson deformation theory. We prove that the log-canonical part $π_0$ of $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ is $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-log-symplectic if and only if the pair $(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)$ of Belavin--Drinfeld triples is aperiodic. In this case, we show that $π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)}$ is a maximal $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-invariant Poisson deformation of $π_0$, and we construct a $\mathbb{T}_{(\mathbfΓ^r,\mathbfΓ^c)}$-equivariant Poisson birational map between $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},π_0)$ and $(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times m},π_{(\bar{\mathbfΓ}^r,\bar{\mathbfΓ}^c)})$.

papers.title: Analytic Tools and Weighted Composition Operators on Paley--Wiener Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a scale-explicit analytic framework for operator-theoretic problems on the Paley--Wiener spaces $B_σ^p$, $σ>0$, throughout the full range $0<p\leq\infty$. Using localized Paley--Wiener packets, we obtain sharp-order point-evaluation estimates, quantitative separation of distinct point-evaluation functionals, sampling estimates, and Carleson measure characterizations. As a principal application, we develop a comprehensive theory of weighted composition operators $W_{ψ,\varphi}:B_σ^p\to B_τ^q$, $0<p,q\leq\infty$, $σ,τ>0$. Boundedness forces every nonconstant symbol to be affine with real slope. A sharp dichotomy appears: when $p\leq q$, the weight is governed by the residual bandwidth $τ-σ|a|$; when $q<p$, the weight must also supply the missing integrability, with exponent $pq/(p-q)$, and boundedness coincides with compactness. We also obtain compactness criteria and essential-norm estimates, characterize differences of weighted composition operators via a no-cancellation principle for distinct symbols, and determine the connected and path-connected components of the corresponding operator spaces.

papers.title: Reflection Character Varieties in $\mathrm{SL}_{\pm}(n,\mathbb{R})$ for $2$-Perfect Labeled Truncation Polytopes
papers.abstract: A truncation polytope is a combinatorial polytope represented by a convex polytope obtained from a simplex by a finite sequence of vertex truncations. Marquis studied the deformation spaces of labeled truncation $3$-polytopes, and Choi-Lee-Marquis studied the $2$-perfect case in higher dimensions. In this paper, we consider Coxeter groups associated with non-simplex $2$-perfect labeled truncation $d$-polytopes with connected Coxeter diagrams, where $d\ge3$. For $n\ge d+1$, we study their reflection-generated representations in $\mathrm{SL}_{\pm}(n,\mathbb{R})$ satisfying Vinberg's conditions. Their images in the real GIT quotients of the full representation spaces under conjugation define the reflection character varieties. These varieties and their subspaces of strict characters are semialgebraic, and we determine their common dimension whenever strict characters exist. We also decompose these subspaces by Cartan matrix rank, show that the nonempty pieces are smooth manifolds, and compute their dimensions explicitly.

papers.title: Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a maximum weight independent set in a graph embedded in a surface of bounded genus and with a bounded number of vertex-disjoint odd faces. In particular, we obtain an algorithm for graphs with an even-faced embedding in a torus and for planar graphs with a bounded number of odd faces, answering a question of Thomassé (2018) and a question of Choi, Gorsky, Kim, McFarland, and Wiederrecht (2025) respectively. We reduce the original problem to finding a minimum cost non-negative integer circulation with homology constraints in the dual of a certain double cover of the original graph.

papers.title: Quasi-locality and weak containment for Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We establish two characterisations of Property A for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry. Such a space has Property A if and only if its Roe algebra coincides with its quasi-local algebra, and if and only if the canonical map from its maximal Roe algebra to its reduced Roe algebra is injective. Both characterisations hold in the uniform and ordinary Roe settings. We also prove, without assuming Property A, that strong quasi-locality is equivalent to norm approximability by finite-propagation operators. In particular, the strongly quasi-local algebra always coincides with the Roe algebra. As applications, we show that a discrete group is exact whenever its full group $C^*$-algebra has the local lifting property, and that the maximal injective crossed-product functor agrees with the reduced crossed-product functor precisely for exact discrete groups.

papers.title: Dimension-free spectral laws and the risk of spectral filters
papers.abstract: Spectral properties of the sample covariance are key to modern machine learning with high-dimensional data. Random matrix theory (RMT) supplies powerful tools; however, most classical results assume proportional asymptotics, where $d/n$ tends to a finite limit. In functional data analysis and kernel methods, a fixed infinite-dimensional Hilbert space is often the more natural setting for the observations, beyond the scope of proportional asymptotics. This calls for a dimension-free spectral theory for i.i.d. observations $\boldsymbol{x}_1, \dots, \boldsymbol{x}_n$ in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with trace-class population covariance $Σ$. Building on the dimension-free ridge regression analysis of Cheng and Montanari (2024), we establish two deterministic equivalents with explicit nonasymptotic error bounds. The first approximates the empirical spectral law $\widehatμ_n$ of the sample Gram matrix by a deterministic law $μ_n$. The second characterizes the conditional prediction risk of analytic spectral filters in linear regression. Previous sharp approximations to prediction risk in this setting have focused on ridge regression and closely-related problems. Our analysis covers a broader class of filters at the bulk scale, with an explicit user-friendly spectral stability condition to check. We apply our theory to power and critical spectral laws, and we recover the proportional regime. For prediction, we study (negative) ridge estimators, iterated ridge, and gradient flow. Mathematically, building on the idea of stochastic interpolation, we construct a deterministic backward path to interpolate the spectral parameter. The resulting bounds on resolvent and mixed-resolvent traces give mesoscopic approximations to the spectral law within the bulk and, by Cauchy's formula, deterministic equivalents for the prediction variance and squared bias of analytic spectral filters.

papers.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
papers.abstract: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

papers.title: Finite presentations for Thompson monoids
papers.abstract: Thompson's group $V$ was introduced in 1965 as one of the first examples of an infinite finitely presented simple group. The Higman-Thompson groups $V_{k, r}$ naturally generalize $V$; they exhibit many of the same interesting properties and have been extensively studied in the literature. Monoid theoretic analogues $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ of the Higman-Thompson groups were first considered by Thompson, and published many years later in work of Birget. The monoid theoretic analogue of the symmetric group is the full transformation monoid, in that every monoid is isomorphic to a submonoid of some full transformation monoid. The analogous role for inverse monoids is played by the symmetric inverse monoid. Birget's three monoids $TV_{k, r}$, $PTV_{k, r}$, and $IV_{k, r}$ are to $V_{n, r}$ what the full, and partial transformation monoids, and the symmetric inverse monoid are to the symmetric group. The second author and De Witt recently showed that $TV_{k, r}$ is finitely presented. In this paper we show that the remaining two monoids $PTV_{k, r}$ and $IV_{k, r}$ are also finitely presented.

papers.title: Infinite projections and failure of pure infiniteness in simple nuclear $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a separable, unital, simple, nuclear $C^*$-algebra in the UCT class such that every nonzero projection in its stabilization is infinite, while it contains a nonzero projectionless hereditary subalgebra. The construction gives a negative answer to the question whether infiniteness of all nonzero projections in a unital simple nuclear $C^*$-algebra implies pure infiniteness.

papers.title: Weak error of approximation of a Lévy-type process using dynamic cutting
papers.abstract: In this note we consider, on one hand, the implementation of the parametrix method for estimation of the distance between functionals $\Ee^x f(X_t)$ and $\Ee^x f(\widetilde X_t)$ of two Lévy-type processes $X$ and $\tilde X$. On the other hand, we estimate the weak error appearing by substituting small jumps by a (time-inhomogeneous) diffusion. Both methods rely on the time-dependent cutting procedure, designed to remove small jumps in a time-dependent way.

papers.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

papers.title: Simultaneous reconstruction of an obstacle and its wavenumber for the Helmholtz equation: a robust optimization approach
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to recover simultaneously the shape and wavenumber of an object from noisy radar or sonar measurements. The physical problem is modeled in a bounded domain with the Helmholtz equation and appropriate transmission conditions. The approach relies on a Kohn-Vogelius formulation of the inverse problem and uses Nesterov's accelerated gradient descent combined with shape optimization techniques. To address the robustness of the method with respect to measurement noise, we are looking to minimize a convex combination of the expected value and variance, which we achieve by using a Karhunen-Lo{è}ve expansion. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through twodimensional numerical experiments.

papers.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
papers.abstract: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk. We also prove a Weyl law of the capacities for all toric domains in dimension $2n$. The algebraic verification is based on a chain model for the Chiu-Tamarkin complex of all toric domains in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, which recovers Irie's conjectural chain model of $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology for star-shaped toric domains (defined only) in $\mathbb{R}^4$.

papers.title: A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
papers.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz. In particular the answer is negative for general finite-energy data, and the open question is reduced to Lipschitz data.

papers.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
papers.abstract: It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward. We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree. More precisely, for the pullback of a Lie groupoid along a surjective submersion, we construct an explicit cochain-level homotopy inverse to the natural pullback map. We first treat Čech groupoids, where the construction only involves a partition of unity, and then extend it to arbitrary surjective submersions, for which the extra choice of local sections is needed. We also show that the resulting operators preserve the complexes associated with $\mathcal{VB}$-groupoids, including homogeneous and $\mathcal{VB}$-cochains. As an application, we obtain explicit transfer maps for deformation cocycles of Morita equivalent Lie groupoids and recover the Morita invariance of deformation cohomology.

papers.title: Full-Cover and Non-Overlapping Uni-domination in Graphs: Bounds and Complexity
papers.abstract: A vertex is uni-dominated by a set $S \subseteq V(G)$ if exactly one vertex of $S$ lies in its closed neighborhood, and the uni-domination number $\mathrm{ud}^*(G)$ is the largest number of vertices a single set can uni-dominate. The graphs admitting an efficient dominating set are those with $\mathrm{ud}^*(G) = n$. Hedetniemi and Rall asked for the largest constant $c$ with $\mathrm{ud}^*(T) \geq c \cdot n$ for every tree $T$ of order $n$. We answer their question: the constant is $4/5$, and a set attaining it can be computed in linear time. This set is moreover a dominating set. Recall that an efficient dominating set satisfies two requirements at once: it dominates every vertex, and it dominates no vertex twice. Our set satisfies the first one, which leads us to study $\mathrm{ud}^*$ under each of the two requirements separately, giving the Full-Cover variant $\mathrm{ud}^*_0$ and the Non-Overlapping variant $\mathrm{ud}^*_+$. The two behave very differently: on arbitrarily large graphs $\mathrm{ud}^*_0$ may remain bounded by a constant, whereas $\mathrm{ud}^*_+$ always grows with the order. We present bounds for both, and show that the associated decision problems are polynomial for constant thresholds and NP-complete for the thresholds $\lceil \sqrt[c]{n} \rceil$ and $4\sqrt{n}$, respectively, the latter even on split graphs. Finally, we show that neither of the two parameters bounds the other.

papers.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
papers.abstract: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports. We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the Künneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

papers.title: Zeta Functions of Polygonal Numbers: Analytic Continuation, Poles and Zero Scattering
papers.abstract: We study the Zeta functions associated with polygonal numbers, focusing on their meromorphic continuation, poles, residues, and trivial zeros. We then investigate the distribution of their nontrivial zeros. Under explicit hypotheses, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean real part of zeros in long height windows. The formula predicts convergence of this mean to 1/4 as the height tends to infinity. We also formulate a stronger concentration conjecture and examine numerical evidence for it.

papers.title: Möbius-Pseudorandomness for Algebraic Circuits
papers.abstract: We define a notion of Möbius-pseudorandomness for integer sequences generated by multivariate polynomials computed by small and simple algebraic circuits. This mirrors a related definition of Kalai that concerns boolean functions computed by small boolean circuits. We then prove Möbius-pseudorandomness results for polynomials computed by algebraic circuits with few multiplication gates (of any depth), for polynomials with small-dimensional partial derivative space, and for the determinant and permanent. We conjecture that these results hold in general for polynomial-size algebraic circuits.

papers.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{E}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$ and let $μ$ be a nonnegative finitely additive $σ$-finite measure on the Borel $σ$-algebra of $G$ whose values on $\mathscr{E}$ are finite but unbounded. Applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{μ(B\cap E)}{μ(E)}\right\}_{E\in \mathscr{E}}$ yields a finitely additive measure $\varphi_μ$, which can be viewed as a generalized normalization of $μ$ to total mass one. To obtain a nontrivial necessary condition on $μ$ for the resulting measure $\varphi_μ$ to be invariant, we establish two results of independent interest: we extend the Yosida--Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $σ$-finite measures and prove a theorem previously stated by Bingham and Ostaszewski concerning translates of sets of Haar measure zero. The first theorem yields a decomposition of $μ$ into a purely finitely additive component and two countably additive components, respectively singular and absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure. Using the second result, we show that the invariance of $\varphi_μ$ implies that the singular component $μ_s$ is negligible relative to $μ$ and can be removed without changing $\varphi_μ$. A counterexample demonstrates that the purely finitely additive component $μ_p$ need not have these properties.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
papers.abstract: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture. Both Green's Conjecture and the Secant Conjecture are know to be true in the generic case, as well as in many other situations.

papers.title: On Mean Field Games with Focusing Logarithmic Local Couplings
papers.abstract: In this note we study the existence theory of classical solutions to a second order stationary discounted Mean Field Games (MFG) system with focusing logarithmic local coupling in one space dimension. We then show the convergence of classical solutions to the discounted stationary MFG system in the large discount/cheap control limit in the spirit of the work of Bardi--Cardaliaguet.

papers.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
papers.abstract: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for the Nodal Measure of Clamped Plate Eigenfunctions in Smooth Domains
papers.abstract: We investigate measure estimates for the nodal sets of nonzero real eigenfunctions $u$ of the biharmonic operator, satisfying $Δ^2u=λu$ in $Ω$ with clamped boundary conditions $u=\partial_νu=0$ on $\partialΩ$. We establish the optimal upper bound of order $λ^{1/4}$ for the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of their nodal sets on general bounded connected $C^\infty$ domains. Our approach combines an enhanced annular Carleman estimate with propagation of mass along a finite chain of balls, these yield a doubling index bounded uniformly up to the boundary.Interior analyticity then gives the nodal measure away from the boundary.
