For these we apply the O'Nan--Scott theorems for primitive and for quasiprimitive permutation groups and prove that the automorphism group of every such design is almost simple on points and on blocks. Together with the classification of finite simple groups, this classifies all non-symmetric block-primitive $2$-designs except for two families of block stabilizers in even characteristic. The exceptions are as follows. One family is of subfield type, $PSL_2(q_0)$ with $q=q_0^{d}$, $d\geq2$, of order below the dihedral point stabilizer $D_{2(q\pm1)}$, and includes $S_3\cong PSL_2(2)$ and $A_5\cong PSL_2(4)$. The other is the dihedral block stabilizer $D_{2(q-1)}$, where the block is a union of $a$ of the $q/2$ orbits, so that $v=q(q-1)/2$, $k=a(q-1)$ and $λ=2a(aq-a-1)/(q-2)$, the last an integer exactly when $(q-2)/2$ divides $a(a-1)$; this family is exhausted by finite enumeration except at the degrees beyond its range. We then determine which of these designs have strength $t\geq 3$. Apart from the inversive planes and the five Witt designs, exactly two Steiner families arise, attached to the exceptional maximal subgroups of $PGL_2(q)$. There is no non-complete design of strength $t\geq 6$.

papers.title: Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
papers.abstract: The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for Lévy operators on nilpotent and compact Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a left-invariant Lévy operator, with characteristics $(a,b,μ)$, on a connected and simply connected Lie group $G$ that is either compact or nilpotent with $[G,[G,G]]$ relatively compact (equivalently, of step at most two). We prove that every bounded distributional solution of $\mathcal{L}u=0$ is right-invariant under the closed subgroup $P=\overline{\langle\exp\mathfrak h_0\cup\text{supp}μ\rangle}$, where $\mathfrak h_0=\text{Lie}\langle b,\operatorname{ran}(a)\rangle$, and is constant if and only if $P=G$. In the compact case we give three proofs, one through the Itô--Kawada equidistribution theorem, one by propagation of the maximum and one by an application of the Peter-Weyl theorem, while the nilpotent case rests on the Choquet--Deny theorem of Bénard and Frisch.

papers.title: Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Stationary Convective Brinkman--Forchheimer Extended Darcy Equations with a Nonlinear Slip Boundary Condition of Friction Type
papers.abstract: This work develops and analyzes several discontinuous Galerkin methods for a variational inequality associated with the stationary convective Brinkman--Forchheimer extended Darcy (CBFeD) system. The CBFeD model generalizes the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations by incorporating additional damping and pumping terms. The resulting variational inequality characterizes the motion of a viscous, incompressible fluid in a saturated porous medium under a friction-type slip boundary condition. For the CBFeD variational inequality, we first explore the existence of a unique weak solution. Then, we establish the existence, uniqueness, and stability of the numerical solutions obtained using discontinuous Galerkin methods. Optimal error estimates are derived, measured in the broken $H^1$-norm for the velocity and in the $L^2$-norm for the pressure, when linear velocity elements and piecewise constant pressure approximations are employed. Numerical simulations are carried out to confirm the theoretically predicted convergence orders and to highlight key strengths of the method, including its ability to capture discontinuities, effectively resolve shear layers, handle advection-dominated regimes, and operate robustly on general polygonal meshes.

papers.title: Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\), \[S_n(t)=Ω_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

papers.title: On VMO-Type Characterizations of Ball Banach Sobolev Spaces and Independence of Integrable Index of Special John--Nirenberg--Campanato Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, $X$ be a ball Banach function space, and $W^{k,X}$ denote the corresponding ball Banach Sobolev space. In this article, we solve six questions in [Math. Z. 311 (2025)]. Specifically, we first prove that the constants in its VMO-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ are sharp uniformly over all ball Banach function spaces satisfying suitable assumptions. Next, we show that the BBM-type formula and the BSVY-type formula involving minimizing polynomials or ball averages fail in general. In contrast, we establish higher-order BBM-type formulas involving Taylor polynomials and further obtain a Taylor-type characterization of $W^{k,X}$ under suitable assumptions. Moreover, we construct counterexamples to show that the characterization of $W^{k,X}$ via higher-order minimizing polynomials fails in general. Finally, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for special John--Nirenberg--Campanato spaces defined via congruent cubes to be independent of their integrability exponent $q$.

papers.title: Markov potential priors for prediction in Gamma models
papers.abstract: We consider Bayesian prediction in independent Gamma scale models with arbitrary known positive shape parameters. When the dimension is at least three, we construct a shrinkage prior toward any prespecified positive scale vector. The resulting predictive density strictly dominates the Jeffreys predictive density under Kullback--Leibler loss and is minimax. The prior is obtained by weighting the Jeffreys prior with a Markov potential. The transition is determined by the beta--gamma decomposition. The domination result is nonasymptotic.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Jordan tuple conjecture of Ball and Helton
papers.abstract: This article constructs a pair of bounded commuting 3-symmetric operators with no Jordan-family extension. The operators are coordinate multipliers on a Sobolev space of functions with values in three dimensional complex Euclidean space with an equivalent Hilbert norm. Their quadratic symbol has no operator polynomial factorization, even with an auxiliary target Hilbert space. The construction transfers the nonfactorability of the matrix quadratic used by Russo to the symbol of a commuting 3-symmetric tuple. The factorization approach of McCullough--Russo and Russo then supplies the obstruction to a Jordan-family extension.

papers.title: A generic $p$-Wasserstein space is isometrically rigid
papers.abstract: We prove for any parameter $p \geq 1$ that the $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ of a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X)$ is isometrically rigid, that is, its isometries are precisely the push-forwards of the isometries of $(X,d_X).$ We also study the question whether the isometry class of a $p$-Wasserstein space completely determines the isometry class of the underlying space. We prove for any $p\geq 1$ that for a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X),$ its $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ is isometric to another $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(Y,d_Y)$ if and only if $(Y,d_Y)$ is isometric to $(X,d_X).$ En route we prove that a stronger property, which we call the Dirac preservation property, is also generic.

papers.title: Bumpless pipe dreams for involutions and shifted plane partitions
papers.abstract: This article studies a triangular variant of bumpless pipe dreams for involutions in the symmetric group. We prove that a natural weight generating function for these objects recovers all involution Schubert polynomials. For vexillary involutions, we derive a $K$-theoretic extension of this result that gives a new formula for orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials. In the course of showing this formula, we compute a diagonal term order Gröbner basis for the defining ideals of symmetric matrix Schubert varieties associated to vexillary involutions. As applications, we prove a conjectured product formula for principal specializations of involution Schubert polynomials. We go on to derive a shifted analogue of the Fomin--Kirillov formula counting bounded plane partitions. This analogue proves the straight-shape case of a conjecture of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova on the Ehrhart positivity for the order polytopes of shifted partitions. We also conjecture a bumpless pipe dream formula for involution Grothendieck polynomials and discuss connections with diagonally symmetric alternating sign matrices and asymptotics of principal specializations.

papers.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
papers.abstract: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

papers.title: On complemented skew braces
papers.abstract: We investigate complemented skew left braces, that is, skew braces in which every skew subbrace admits a complement. We establish that if every minimal subbrace of a finite skew brace is complemented, then the brace is supersoluble and all its skew subbraces of prime power order are elementary abelian. We also show that the converse does not hold in general, providing a finite counterexample. Furthermore, we prove that every subbrace of a finite direct product of square-free skew braces is complemented. Finally, we extend our investigation to the infinite setting, proving that every multipermutational complemented skew brace is hypercyclic and that all its skew subbraces whose additive groups are $p$-groups are elementary abelian.

papers.title: Enforcing Ellipsoidal Constraints in Neural Networks with a Polynomial Safety Layer
papers.abstract: Often the output of a learned mapping must satisfy prescribed constraints. In the control of autonomous systems, for example, the chosen action must keep the system within a collision-free region. We consider the case in which a proposed output is corrected by projection onto a safety ellipsoid. Computing this projection amounts to solving a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). We construct a neural-network safety layer by unrolling a feasibility-preserving polynomial penalty iteration. The unrolled structure allows the loss gradient to propagate from the feasible output through the safety layer to the network parameters during training. We show how to choose the layer parameters so that every iterate is feasible and give a computable bound on its distance to the exact projection at any prescribed depth. We illustrate the method by training a LiDAR-based policy to control an unmanned aerial vehicle. A privileged model predictive control expert uses the map and the measured vehicle state to generate the training data. In the simulated narrow mazes, the filtered policy avoided wall contact at every tested stage of training, including at initialization, when every unfiltered flight hit a wall. A representative build of the learned policy and its safety layer for an Arm Cortex-M4F microcontroller occupies about 36 KiB of flash, with a RAM budget below 5 KiB.

papers.title: Local limit theorem for branching processes with immigration
papers.abstract: Let $\{Y_{n}, n\geq 0\}$ be a critical branching process with immigration. Under the minimal moment restrictions, namely, assuming finite variance for the number of particles of the offspring and finite mean for the number of immigrating particles, we obtain a local limit theorem for the process $\{Y_{n}\}$.

papers.title: Singular Birth-Death model
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a one-dimensional singular birth-death model constructed from Itô's Brownian excursion measure. In this model, particles are born at the origin at infinite rate, evolve as Brownian excursions away from the origin, and are killed upon returning to the origin. Although the number of particles alive at any fixed deterministic time is almost surely finite, we prove that the set of exceptional times at which infinitely many particles are alive is almost surely dense and has Hausdorff dimension $1/2$. We further investigate the spatial structure of the particle system at such exceptional times. In particular, we identify the critical near-origin profile of the infinite particle cloud, which is governed by a scale of order $\log\log(1/|x|)^{-1}$ as $x\downarrow0$. Finally, we establish laws of large numbers and central limit theorems for two natural observables of the system: the $α$-power sum of the positions of all alive particles and the top particle position.

papers.title: Distance-$2$ isolation of connected graphs
papers.abstract:
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of graphs and $F$ is a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$, then we call $F$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. For a subset $D$ of the vertex set $V(G)$, let $N^2[D]$ denote the second closed neighbourhood of $D$. Let $ι_2(G, \mathcal{F})$ denote the size of a smallest subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $N^2[D]$ intersects the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G - N^2[G]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). For $k \geq 0$, let $\mathcal{E}_k$ denote the set of connected graphs that have at least $k$ edges (and at least one vertex if $k = 0$). By a well-known result of Meir and Moon, $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_0) \leq n/3$ if $n \geq 3$. We show that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_1) \leq n/4$ if $n 
eq 2$, $n 
eq 3$ and $G$ is not a $7$-cycle. Hua and Liu recently showed that if $G$ is not a $4$-vertex path or a $4$-cycle or a $9$-cycle, then there exists a subset $D$ of $V(G)$ such that $|D| \leq n/5$ and each component of $G-N^2[D]$ has a universal vertex. We strengthen this result by showing that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_2) \leq n/5$ if $n 
eq 3$, $n 
eq 4$ and $G$ is not an $8$-cycle or one of five $9$-vertex graphs. It follows that $ι_2(G, \mathcal{E}_3) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph or a $9$-cycle. This also implies the result of Hua and Liu, and that if $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of cycles, then $ι_2(G, \mathcal{C}) \leq n/5$ unless $G$ is a $3$-cycle or a $4$-vertex graph containing a cycle. All these bounds are sharp.

papers.title: A Kreiss theorem for fractional Cauchy problems with a finite slow component
papers.abstract: Fractional Cauchy problems with a Caputo derivative of order bounded by one are solved by Mittag-Leffler operator families that lack the semigroup property but remain bounded for classes of sectorial generators, even with spectrum in the right half-plane. To study their transient growth we introduce the fractional Kreiss constant via the Laplace transform of the propagator family. For a closed generator on a Banach space with a time-scale separation and a finite spectral component, that is, a finite-rank projector commuting with the generator whose complement carries a bounded family, we prove that the projected part of the propagator (typically slow spectral part carrying dynamics that is pertinent at mid and long time-scales) is comparable to a deflated Kreiss constant up to a factor linear in the rank, uniformly in fractional order and independently of the dimension. The analytic core of this result is a Bernstein-type inequality for a class of non-rational functions on vertical lines proved by bounding the turning of the derivative. This is a fundamentally different technique from the classical one used in Kreiss theorem for Markov semigroups based on counting intersections of algebraic curves. Importantly, we show that the rank dependence cannot be removed while keeping the Kreiss constant upper bound. Finally, we show that in Hilbert spaces, generators whose numerical range avoids the sector of instability obey the sharp bound of normal operators, which no spectral-set estimate improves. To conclude, we discuss how subdiffusion driven by a self-excited oscillator, the time-fractional Schrödinger equation, and time-changed Markov dynamics illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Nonparametric Classification under Adversarial Attacks: Decision-Boundary Geometry and Optimal Rates
papers.abstract: Unlike in continuous regression, a small input perturbation in classification can move an input across a decision boundary and flip the predicted label. Decision-boundary geometry is therefore essential to understanding adversarial classification risk. Under anisotropic smoothness and margin conditions, we quantify this geometric contribution and establish sharp minimax rates for adversarial excess risk relative to the ordinary Bayes risk. These rates comprise a statistical term governed by the harmonic mean smoothness and a geometric cost of adversarial perturbations governed by the least smooth direction. As smoothness and the margin exponent vary, the adversarial term exhibits a phase transition from a fractional power of the attack radius to linear scaling, with a logarithmic correction in a critical regime. In addition, we construct an adaptive classifier that attains these rates over a range of smoothness and margin classes. We further characterize the minimax rate for adversarial excess risk under a budget on ordinary excess risk, yielding an explicit trade-off curve. The curve identifies attack regimes where ordinary minimax optimality entails a suboptimal adversarial rate. Finally, numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Motivic Borel-Moore Homology is Borel-Moore Motivic Homology
papers.abstract: This paper studies the higher Chow groups of arbitrary finite type separated schemes using motivic homotopy theory, serving as a Borel-Moore counterpart to the $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology of Bachmann-Elmanto-Morrow. We construct a filtration on the G-theory spectrum of a finite type separated scheme $X$, inducing an Atiyah-Hirzebruch style spectral sequence whose associated graded pieces are a complex computing the higher Chow groups of $X$. We prove that this complex is representable in the stable motivic homotopy category, and is a module over the $\mathbb{A}^1$-motivic complex, giving rise to an action of $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology on the Bloch-Levine cycle complex. This generalizes some results of Bloch and Levine relating higher Chow groups and motivic cohomology to the case of schemes over an arbitrary base, and which need not be smooth or equidimensional.

papers.title: On the nodal set of the second eigenfunction of the Laplacian in convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $Ω$ be a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$. We prove that the closure of the interior nodal set of any second Dirichlet eigenfunction of $Ω$ intersects $\partialΩ$. The proof combines the ground-state derivative and the quantitative log-concavity estimate of Andrews and Clutterbuck with a variational argument.

papers.title: Weak--type $(1,1;\frac{1}{2})$--estimate for the bilinear Bochner--Riesz mean at the critical index
papers.abstract: We prove the weak-type estimate at the end-point $\big(1,1,\frac{1}{2}\big)$ for the bilinear Bochner--Riesz mean at the critical index $α_c=n-\frac{1}{2}$ in all dimensions $n\geq 1$. Our proof is motivated by Christ's method for the linear Bochner--Riesz operator at the critical index. We develop a bilinear analogue of the $TT^*$ method to address the end-point boundedness of the bilinear Bochner--Riesz operator. This approach provides a useful tool in addressing the end-point issues for bilinear operators.

papers.title: Global Hyperbolicity Criterion for Regular Sub-Lorentzian Manifolds
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global hyperbolicity of regular sub-Lorentzian manifolds. We establish a criterion for global hyperbolicity on complete Riemannian manifolds, formulated in terms of a smooth time function and an admissible growth function. The proof relies on the theory of differential inclusions. The proposed condition relaxes the classical requirements on the differential of the time function. The effectiveness of the obtained criterion is illustrated on classical nonholonomic structures: the Grushin space, the Heisenberg group, and step-2 Carnot groups, for which we find explicit asymptotic bounds on the expansion rate of causal cones that guarantee the preservation of global hyperbolicity.

papers.title: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes
papers.abstract: We prove that the discrete Bilinear Hilbert Transform along the primes, \begin{align} \mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{P}}(f,g)(x) := \sum_{n \neq 0} \frac{Λ(|n|)}{n} f(x-n) g(x+n), \qquad Λ(n) := \begin{cases} \log p & \text{ if } n = p^k, \ k \geq 1 \\ 0 & \text{ otherwise} \end{cases} \end{align} extends to a bounded operator from $\ell^p \times \ell^q \to \ell^r$ whenever $p,q \in (1,\infty)$ and $\frac{1}{r}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}$ in the Banach range, $r \geq 1$, and a particular portion of the quasi-Banach range $r \in \left(\frac{2}{3},1\right)$; in the diagonal case, this extends up to the endpoint $(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{6})$. After $U^3$-based reductions, the philosophy of the proof becomes similar to that of Krause-Mirek-Tao (on different bilinear operators in discrete harmonic analysis), namely a ``splitting" of the problem into an arithmetic component, handled by analysis within cyclic subgroups, and an analytic component, handled by analysis along arithmetic progressions. For the arithmetic component, we draw upon previous work of most of the authors on Carleson operators along the primes; the main analytic input are estimates for UMD space-valued bilinear singular integrals with modulation invariance, due to Di Plinio-Li-Martikainen-Vuorinen.

papers.title: On divisible domains of the flat affine space with parallel volume
papers.abstract: We consider a domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ divisible by a discrete subgroup $Γ$ of the unimodular affine group $\operatorname{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})\ltimes\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that $Ω=\mathbb{R}^d$ if $Γ$ is virtually solvable or if its linear holonomy is virtually contained in a semisimple Lie subgroup of real rank one. In particular, we establish the Kleinian Markus conjecture in both cases.

papers.title: Gradient-Based Co-Design of Systems and Reinforcement Learning Policies with Differentiable Simulators
papers.abstract: Co-design is the problem of jointly optimizing the design of a system and the policy that operates it. Neither can be chosen independently: a system design is only as good as the policy trained for it, and the optimal policy changes with the design. When that policy is learned by reinforcement learning (RL), evaluating a candidate design requires a full policy training run, and the design is usually optimized by black-box search such as Bayesian optimization (BO) or evolution strategies (ES). These methods scale poorly with the design dimension and ignore the differentiable structure of modern simulators and, in particular, the sensitivity of the optimal policy with respect to the design. We instead derive a gradient-based co-design method, where the design gradient decomposes into a direct effect of changing the design at a fixed policy and an indirect effect through the design-dependent optimal policy. The indirect effect requires the sensitivity of the converged policy to the design, which we obtain by applying the implicit function theorem to the stationarity condition of the policy gradient. Based on this sensitivity, we develop a proof-of-concept co-design algorithm with stochastic value gradient (SVG)-style policy optimization, prove that it converges to an approximately stationary design, and demonstrate on a differentiable networked-system benchmark with high-dimensional design spaces that it consistently outperforms BO and ES.

papers.title: When the Boundary Changes the Bulk: Topological Edge Modes in Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: For dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in open chains it has been noted that the boundary can change the bulk: in time windows bounded by DQPTs, exponentially localized edge modes of the Loschmidt matrix produce a finite change in the intensive return rate. These modes have been attributed to topological properties of the initial and final Hamiltonians. Here we show that it is not the topology of the Hamiltonians but rather that of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix which protects these edge modes. In particular, we show that topological edge modes can exist in class A, where both Hamiltonians are topologically trivial. For classes A, BDI, and AIII we show that these modes are protected by $\mathbb{Z}$ indices of a Toeplitz operator and that K-splitting theorems provide a precise bulk-boundary correspondence. In class D, they are protected instead by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ index that records whether the quench has flipped the fermion parity at the edge. The bulk invariant for class D can be formulated either as a ratio of the Loschmidt amplitudes for periodic and anti-periodic boundary conditions or as a winding number that counts phase vortices in momentum and time. We discuss examples and provide numerical data for all four topological classes.

papers.title: On the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue 1 of a graph
papers.abstract: A connected graph $G$ with $n\ge 2$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges is called a \emph{$k$-cyclic graph} if $k=\varepsilon-n+1$. The Laplacian matrix is defined as $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. Let $m_{G}(1)$ be the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue $1$ of $G$. In this paper, we show that for fixed integers $n\ge \big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil$ and $k\geq0$, if $G$ is a $k$-cyclic graph of order $n$, then \begin{equation*} \displaystyle m_{G}(1)\leq n-\big\lceil\frac{3+\sqrt{8k+1}} {2}\big\rceil \end{equation*} and moreover, we completely characterize all extremal graphs attained the upper bound.

papers.title: Structural latent dimension: deterministic geometry and local Fisher structure
papers.abstract: We study the structural dimension of a second-order object: the minimum latent dimension that remains necessary relative to a declared class of competing dependence. Building on minimum-rank factor analysis and low-rank-plus-sparse decomposition, we use distances to lower-dimensional classes to describe inference near structural ambiguity. General distance and tangent-cone facts yield confidence statements and local margins. For rank-zero competitors with bounded residual degree, we derive exact maximum-weight $b$-matching formulas, support-slack tangent cones and sparse-spike angles; a shared residual support across a field can produce separation absent pointwise. We give positive-semidefinite brackets, a dimension-free Gaussian likelihood expansion, an exact quotient by the tangent of a low-rank background, and a detection floor from the margin. Equal-angle configurations with different branch multiplicities motivate static and spectral detection conjectures. Joint low-rank/residual profiling and the sharp composite information boundaries remain open.

papers.title: An ancient diophantine problem of Brahmagupta
papers.abstract: In the seventh century CE, Brahmagupta gave a parametric solution to the problem of finding two numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x+y, x-y$ and $xy+1$ are all squares. We describe a method for generating infinitely many rational parametric solutions of the problem and another method for generating parametric solutions of the problem in terms of univariate polynomials with integer coefficients. The complete solution of the problem still remains elusive.

papers.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Positive Bounded Solutions for Semilinear Dirichlet Problems in Exterior-Star Domains
papers.abstract: We prove the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive bounded solutions for the Dirichlet problem $$-Δu=f(u)\,\ \ \text{in}\ \ Ω, \ \ u=0\,\ \ \text{on}\ \ \partialΩ,$$ where $f$ is a positive reaction and $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a uniformly $C^{2,γ}$ domain with a star-shaped complement. Our uniqueness result gives a positive answer to Open Question 1 of [H. Berestycki and C. Graham, ARMA, 2026].

papers.title: The Common-Color Spectrum of Endpoint Set-Coloring Ramsey Numbers
papers.abstract: The set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s,t)$ is the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to each edge of $K_N$ contains a $K_n$ whose edge labels have at least $t$ common colors. Motivated by the work of Erdős and Szemerédi on $R(n;r,r-1,1)$, we write $R(n;r,r-1,t)=\exp\bigl(nf_{r,n}(t)\bigr)$ and study $f(t):=f_{r,n}(t)$ as $t$ ranges from $1$ to $r-1$. For fixed integers $r\ge2$ and $1\le t<r$, we prove that, as $n\to\infty$, \( \frac12\log\frac{r}{r-t}+o(1) \le f(t) \le \frac{r}{r-t}\log\frac{r}{r-t} +C+O_{r,t}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \) where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. Comparisons between different numbers of colors show that the rates $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}f_{r,n}(t)$, defined for fixed $r$ and $t$, each have a limit as $r\to\infty$ and $\frac{t}{r}\toα\in(0,1)$ from above. The resulting two functions of $α$ are finite, positive, nondecreasing, and right-continuous. Writing $Δ_t=f(t+1)-f(t)$, we further prove that, as $r\to\infty$, uniformly for $n\ge r^2$, at least $\frac{(1-o(1))\log r}{\log\log r}$ indices $1\le t<\frac{r}{2}$ satisfy $Δ_t\ge\frac{1-o(1)}{2r}$. For $r,n\ge3$ and $2\le h\le r-1$, the final $h-1$ increments account for at least $1-\frac{1}{\left\lceil h/2\right\rceil}$ of the total increase $f(r-1)-f(1)$. For each fixed $r\ge4$, the last increment has a positive lower limit as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, for $r,n\ge3$, it exceeds the sum of all preceding increments whenever $r$ is even or $n=3$.

papers.title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$
papers.abstract: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism split into four families, each in bijection with $\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. Every other realizable endomorphism sends both standard generators to reflections. For each such endomorphism, the realizable multipliers on $π_2(M)\cong\mathbb{Z}$ are precisely the odd integers $d$, and the classes with fixed multiplier are in bijection with $\mathbb Z/|d|\mathbb Z$ after choosing a reference homotopy class. We compute an explicit composition law on the double-reflection submonoid and determine the pointed self-homotopy equivalences. The classes inducing the trivial fundamental-group endomorphism form a subset $\mathcal{T}$ that is preserved by composition on either side with arbitrary pointed homotopy classes and satisfies $\mathcal{T}^2=\{0\}$, where $0$ is the constant class. For each fixed triple $(m,k,d)$ in the double-reflection case, the $|d|$ classes induce identical homomorphisms on every homotopy group. Thus the secondary invariant detects distinctions invisible to these induced homomorphisms.

papers.title: Finding Low-Energy States of the Bernasconi Model via Simulated Transverse-Field Quantum Dynamics
papers.abstract: The Low-Autocorrelation Binary Sequence (LABS) problem, the ground-state problem of the Bernasconi model, has a rugged landscape with deep, isolated local minima. We study real-time transverse-field dynamics initialized in these minima as a means of reaching lower-energy configurations. Using GPU statevector simulation for N = 20-30 spins, we compare the escape probability per verified quantum sample with the success rate per energy evaluation of steepest-descent kicks, random restarts and tabu search. Using the same field and sampling window across all system sizes, we find that, relative to the best classical baseline, the sampler achieves a factor of 11.9-35.2 for the deepest traps and 13.4-27.2 for the next energy tier. These ratios describe a constant-factor improvement in sample efficiency over the sizes studied. At the adopted field, broad Hamming-space spreading coexists with a strong preference for low-energy states. This regime follows a sharp increase in displacement as the field is raised. To connect this behaviour to the landscape, a short-time expansion relates the onset of escape to target distance and intermediate energies. Bounds on isotropic spin flips and on the free transverse mixer quantify the role of the Bernasconi potential in the observed transfer. At N = 28, the ground-state probability at t = 30 exceeds a canonical cost prediction fitted to the same mean energy by a factor of about 1.9. The cost of generating each quantum sample is assessed separately through a hardware estimate, which places a direct circuit implementation two to three orders of magnitude beyond present processor capabilities.

papers.title: Repairing actuator schedules under graph constraints
papers.abstract: We consider a discrete-time linear system in which each actuator is assigned to one time slot. A graph $H$ records which pairs of actuators cannot share a slot. We seek to remove conflicts by exchanging actuators between slots, while preserving all tail reachability spaces. These spaces describe the terminal corrections available from each time slot onward. We give a sufficient condition based on the number of exchanges that preserve the required bases. The condition guarantees repair from every compatible starting schedule. Two bounds for checking it use failed basis tests and dependent column selections. Each accepted exchange reduces the conflict count, so the procedure uses at most as many exchanges as there are initial conflicts. An explicit family with unequal rank increments admits repair when $3N>4Δ(H)+4$, where $Δ(H)$ is the largest number of forbidden partners of any actuator. We also give a family of two-slot examples with only one forbidden partner per actuator and two initial conflicts. The basis constraints force every strict improvement to move arbitrarily many actuators, although one exchange suffices without those constraints. A second example has a connected conflict graph and one initial conflict.

papers.title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
papers.abstract: We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other. For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.

papers.title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Turán numbers and beyond
papers.abstract: The Hadwiger-Debrunner number $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)$ is defined as the maximum piercing number over all finite families of compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ in which among every $p$ sets, some $q$ have non-empty intersection. We develop three complementary constructions that improve lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. For any fixed $q>d\ge 2$, a randomly sparsified family of hyperplanes, analyzed using hypergraph containers, yields $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)\ge p^{(d+q-2)/(q-1)+o(1)}$ as $p\rightarrow\infty$. To deduce further bounds, we establish a transfer argument from upper bounds on the sizes of sufficiently general-positioned subsets of high-dimensional integer grids to lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. Two methodologies are adopted to derive the former: one connects rainbow Turán theory and general-positioned grid sets, and the other uses full spark linear reduction of tuples with bounded-size preimages. As a combinatorial ingredient, we describe the rainbow Turán behavior under suspension operations, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: DLR variational principle for the one-dimensional log-gas and another proof of existence of Sine-beta
papers.abstract: We show that every stationary solution of the Dobrushin--Lanford--Ruelle (DLR) equations for the one-dimensional log-gas with a quantitative control on its number variance minimizes the free energy functional. This yields a DLR variational principle for this continuous long-range system. Moreover, we show that any limit point of the finite-volume log-gases is stationary and satisfies this condition. This allows us to give a new, physical proof of the existence of a microscopic limit for the Gaussian Beta Ensembles, known as the Sine-beta point process.

papers.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

papers.title: Lipschitz bounds and gradient continuity for the Trudinger equation
papers.abstract: We establish local spatial Lipschitz and gradient Hölder estimates for general nonnegative weak solutions to Trudinger's equation $\partial_t u^{p-1}=Δ_pu$, $p>1$. The estimates are uniform across the zero set. The proofs combine Bernstein-type estimates for power transformations, smooth approximation, and comparison with exponential barriers near the zero set.

papers.title: Quantum Dynamics of Dynamics
papers.abstract: Quantum channels (in discrete time) and Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) master equations (in continuous time) are the central tools of open quantum systems, but they rest on memoryless approximations (Born, Markov, secular) that fail in many physically relevant settings, most notably non-Markovian dynamics. There, tracking the state alone is insufficient: interventions at intermediate times disturb the environment, so multi-time correlations carry physical information that the state evolution cannot capture. The framework of higher-order quantum operations addresses this by treating controllable operations as \textit{inputs} to a process that maps operations to operations, so that the primitive object is a quantum \textit{dynamics} rather than a quantum \textit{state}. Here, we derive the most general continuous-time, CP-divisible evolution of such an object, the \textit{quantum comb master equation} (QCME), which governs the quantum ``dynamics of dynamics''. Its GKSL-like generator includes encoder--decoder correlation terms coupling distinct temporal interventions. A generalized Born--Markov coarse-graining derivation identifies microscopic conditions for this structure. The QCME yields time-local evolution equations for two-time correlators beyond reduced-state dynamics and extends to more times. We show correlations between Schr"odinger- and Heisenberg-picture evolutions inaccessible to independent GKSL equations, describe quantum-channel evolution motivated by process tomography, and obtain time-local equations for linear response functions and OTOCs under environmental influences.

papers.title: Half-factorial generating sets and the realization of Dedekind class groups
papers.abstract: We prove a cardinality obstruction to realizing an abelian group as the ideal class group of a half-factorial Dedekind domain. If an abelian $p$-group $P$ satisfies $\bigcap_{r\ge1}p^rP=0$ and admits a half-factorial generating subset, then $|P|\le\max\{\aleph_0,|P/pP|\}$. The proof separates generators of equal order by finite quotients. Its group-theoretic ingredient is a direct summand generated by selected members of an arbitrary finite generating set. The torsion subgroup of $\prod_{j\ge1}\mathbb{Z}/p^j\mathbb{Z}$ is uncountable and $p$-adically separated, but has countable quotient modulo $p$; hence it has no half-factorial generating subset. This gives a negative answer to the universal half-factorial Dedekind realization problem for every prime. Pure subgroups give counterexamples of every uncountable cardinality at most the continuum, so the least cardinality of a counterexample is $\aleph_1$. We also study free-kernel lifting, order-preserving lifts across torsion kernels, character-compatible generators, and the failure of compatibility under unions and contraction. These results distinguish global realizability from half-factoriality on bounded subgroups and from integrality of cross numbers.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.

papers.title: A unified cross-scale framework for the dynamic Waddington landscape
papers.abstract: The Waddington epigenetic landscape is a foundational concept in developmental biology, yet its quantitative formulations remain largely disconnected from the population dynamics that originally motivated the metaphor. Existing approaches typically describe either intracellular gene-regulatory dynamics or population-level cell kinetics, but rarely both within a unified framework. Here, we develop a unified PDE-integral framework that couples stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics with probability-conserving population renewal, yielding a dynamic Waddington landscape $U(\vec{x}, t) = -\log f(\vec{x}, t)$ defined directly from the evolving epigenetic probability density $f(\vec{x}, t)$. Rigorous mathematical analysis of this framework establishes its well-posedness and provides conditions for the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions. Application to canonical gene regulatory circuits shows that proliferation is not merely a determinant of population size, but an active regulator of landscape topology. Population renewal reshapes attractor stability and transition barriers in a circuit-dependent manner, generating transient plasticity in some regulatory architectures while stabilizing progenitor states in others. Under highly proliferative conditions, these interactions further produce oscillatory ``breathing'' landscapes. Together, these results establish population renewal as an integral component of cell-fate regulation and extend the Waddington landscape from a static description of intracellular dynamics to a predictive multiscale framework linking gene regulation, cell-state dynamics, and tissue homeostasis.

papers.title: Independent Sets in $C_4$-Free Planar Graphs: Sharp Claw-Free Bounds and Structural Reductions
papers.abstract: For every claw-free $C_4$-free planar graph, we prove the sharp weighted bound $α_w(G)\ge (10/31)\sum_v w(v)$, equivalently $χ_f(G)\le31/10$. The proof uses a line-graph representation and the matching polytope; the exceptional small roots are excluded analytically by planar duality and degree-four neighborhood analysis in triangulations. We also prove that, in every $2$-connected $C_4$-free graph of minimum degree at least four, an independent selection of claw centers leaves a compatible subgraph of noncenters with fractional chromatic number at most three; planarity is not required. We apply these results to the conjecture $α(G)\ge5|V(G)|/16$. A minimum-order counterexample without degree-three vertices has at least forty-nine vertices. When all degree-three components of a minimum counterexample are triangle trees, we derive exact boundary states and a joint matching formula. We identify the remaining deficiency estimate and the additional component types that must be addressed to extend this approach. The general conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Many faces of integer semidefinite programming
papers.abstract: We first establish several properties of integer positive semidefinite matrices, extending known results for binary and ternary positive semidefinite matrices. We then show how to reformulate an integer quadratic program (IQP) as an equivalent integer semidefinite program (ISDP). We distinguish three cases, namely IQPs with two, three, or more than three distinct integer values, and provide several ISDPs for each case. Each reformulation yields either a binary ISDP, a ternary ISDP, or a rescaled version of one of these. The results show that ternary SDP formulations for problems with three distinct integer values provide SDP relaxations with fewer constraints and, in the case of equally spaced integers, also smaller matrix variables than binary-based SDP relaxations. For quadratic problems whose variables can take more than three distinct integer values, one can choose among three formulations based on the size of their matrix variables, the number of constraints, and the strength of the resulting SDP relaxations. We also show how to reformulate a mixed-integer QP as a mixed-integer SDP.

papers.title: Classification problems for diassociative and dendriform algebras: a survey
papers.abstract: Diassociative algebras (associative dialgebras) and dendriform algebras are vector spaces with two binary operations, introduced by J.-L. Loday in the study of Leibniz algebras; their operads are Koszul dual to each other. We survey the classification problem for these two classes, including the Zinbiel algebras, the commutative dendriform algebras, which are Koszul dual to Leibniz algebras. We recall the definitions, the main examples and the Loday diagram with its extension by left-symmetric algebras and dialgebras, and describe the methods used to classify algebras of small dimension: direct computation from lists of associative algebras, annihilator (central) extensions and geometric classification by degenerations. We then collect, by dimension, the known algebraic classifications of diassociative algebras, dendriform algebras and their commutative case, the Zinbiel algebras, point out lists that later work corrected, and summarise the cohomological results that the methods rely on. We close with a list of open problems.

papers.title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
papers.abstract: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.

papers.title: Global dynamics and the diffusive limit of the one-species non-cutoff Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system
papers.abstract: The rigorous derivation of incompressible plasma equations from kinetic plasma models is a fundamental problem in kinetic theory. For the one-species Vlasov--Maxwell--Boltzmann system without angular cutoff, global well-posedness and the diffusive limit have remained largely open in the soft-potential regime. We resolve both problems for $0<s<1$ and $\max\{-3,-\frac32-2s\}<γ<-2s$. For sufficiently small initial perturbations, we construct unique global classical solutions with energy and time-decay estimates uniform in the Knudsen number $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$. The key analytical contribution is a family of coercivity and trilinear estimates for the non-cutoff collision operators with time-dependent quadratic exponential velocity weights. Exploiting conservation of energy in collisions, these estimates combine with weighted interpolation to control the high-order electromagnetic terms despite the slow decay of the electric field. For well-prepared initial data, we prove strong convergence to the incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier--Maxwell system as $\varepsilon\to0$.

papers.title: Spectral Gaps and Low-Energy Modes in Anisotropic High-Contrast PDEs
papers.abstract: We study the low-energy spectrum of high-contrast partial differential equations with strongly anisotropic inclusions. The inclusion stiffness and mass are scaled by a contrast parameter \(η\), while a small material eigenvalue \(ε\) controls anisotropy. Stable extensions of local kernel fields give eigenvalue upper bounds proportional to the inverse contrast, uniformly in anisotropy. Additional low-energy modes arise from fields whose nonzero differential images lie in weak material directions. Each fixed family of compatible weak fields yields additional eigenvalue upper bounds of order $ε+ η^{-1}$, provided a stable extension exists. Under discrete stability assumptions, we obtain corresponding finite element bounds for the weak modes represented by the mesh. For separable scalar diffusion, we prove norm-resolvent convergence to independent background Dirichlet and inclusion Neumann operators as contrast tends to infinity with anisotropy fixed. Numerical experiments for four PDE models illustrate weak modes and mesh-dependent spectral transitions, and scalar diffusion experiments also test spectral decoupling and eigenvalue counting.

papers.title: Fundamental group and $Q$-curvature on open four-manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a complete, connected, and non-compact four-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and nonnegative $Q$-curvature. If $g$ is not Ricci-flat, we show that both the fundamental group $π_1(M)$ and the integral of $Q$-curvature are finite, satisfying $$|π_1(M)|\int_MQ_g dμ_g\leq 8π^2$$ with the equality holding if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(\mathbb{R}^4, e^{2u}|\mathrm{d}x|^2)$ with vanishing isoperimetric ratio.

papers.title: Sum of Powers with Matrix Coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We consider polynomial maps with constants $ω(x,y)=A_1x^k+A_2y^k$ on $M_n(F)$, where $A_1$ is invertible and $k\geq2$. We show that the necessary condition for surjectivity obtained by Saini and Singh (Polynomial maps with constants on matrix algebra, Linear Algebra Appl. 752 (2027), 256-277) is not sufficient in any dimension $n\geq6$. We also completely characterize surjectivity for $n=5$ and $6$.

papers.title: Quadratic Embedding Constants of Block Graphs and Characterization of Cactus-like Graphs
papers.abstract: A (finite or infinite) connected graph is called \textit{cactus-like} if every pair of distinct maximal cliques has at most one vertex in common and its clique graph is a tree. Equivalently, a cactus-like graph is a block graph whose clique graph is a tree. We prove that a finite connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is cactus-like if and only if its quadratic embedding constant satisfies $\mathrm{QEC}(G)<-1/2$. Moreover, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\mathrm{QEC}(G)$ in terms of the clique degree of a block graph $G$. For the proofs, we develop a method for constructing a conditionally negative definite kernel on a block graph by concatenating local kernels along geodesics in the block graph. Concrete examples include free products of complete graphs and trees.

papers.title: Strong Well-Posedness for One-Dimensional Quantile-Dependent SDEs with Hölder-Continuous Diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish strong well-posedness for one-dimensional stochastic differential equations whose drift and diffusion coefficients depend on a prescribed quantile of the solution's marginal law. The diffusion coefficient is uniformly non-degenerate and Hölder continuous in space. The drift is the sum of a non-increasing Hölder-continuous component and a globally Lipschitz component of at most linear growth. Both components are Lipschitz continuous in the quantile variable. The main obstacles are the limited spatial regularity of the diffusion and the quantitative control of quantiles in terms of the $L^1$-distance between densities. We freeze the quantile path and combine uniform Hölder estimates for the resulting densities with a cancellation argument for the second-order diffusion perturbation. This yields an $L^1$-stability estimate for the frozen density flows and, together with uniform tail bounds and positive lower density bounds, a Volterra-type estimate for the frozen quantile map. An exponentially weighted supremum norm makes this map a strict contraction on $[0,T]$, giving a unique self-consistent quantile path and hence a unique strong solution. When the diffusion coefficient is independent of the quantile variable, the Yamada--Watanabe approximation also yields stability with respect to the initial condition.

papers.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
papers.abstract: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic. For $E(n)$-local spectra we express the maps between distinct monochromatic layers of the sphere in terms of the chromatic fracture square. The height-two splitting gives the equality through height two at every prime. For a Noetherian local ring we characterize the Gorenstein property by the form of its closed-point idempotent.

papers.title: Stabilizing Parabolic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: For an irreducible parabolic flat vector bundle of rank $r < 2\sqrt{g}$ on a genus $g$ curve, we prove that an analytically general isomonodromic deformation is stable. This refines Landesman-Litt's semistability result for bundles of rank $< 2\sqrt{g+1}$. The proof applies the non-generically globally generated (non-GGG) lemma to establish infinitesimal obstructions to extending destabilizing subbundles of semistable bundles.

papers.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,ξ)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author.

papers.title: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
papers.abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $ρ_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_tρ=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2ρ)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/ρ$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $Γ$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

papers.title: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
papers.abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we construct simultaneous confidence bands using a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap. Simulation studies evaluate estimation accuracy, the validity of pointwise and uniform inference, and robustness to nuisance model misspecification. A semi-synthetic study calibrated to NHANES illustrates the proposed methods in a setting with a known dose-response function.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference for Multivariate Stable Distributions via LePage Representation with von Mises -- Fisher Spectral Measure
papers.abstract: We develop Bayesian inference for multivariate $α$-stable distributions with von Mises--Fisher spectral measure, motivated by the hitting distribution of Brownian motion on the unit sphere. Inference proceeds via a LePage-type series representation with latent radial, spectral, and Poisson components; truncation bias is absorbed through a Gaussian error term, yielding a likelihood that is smooth in $α\in(0,2)$ with no special treatment at the Cauchy boundary $α=1$. The stability index $α$, spectral concentration $κ$, mean direction $η$, and spectral mass $Γ_\infty$ are estimated jointly by Markov chain Monte Carlo. At the Gaussian boundary $α\to 2$, the limiting covariance matrix equals twice the second moment matrix of the spectral measure, with explicit parametric form determined by $η$ and $κ$; in particular, the anisotropy of the limiting Gaussian distribution is controlled solely by the spectral concentration $κ$. Simulation across $α\in[0.25, 1.99]$ confirms reliable recovery of all parameters.

papers.title: Intersection Cuts for Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programs via Decision-Diagram-Free Sets
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel decision-diagram-based framework for generating intersection cuts to strengthen polyhedral relaxations of bounded mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) with general nonlinear constraints. Building on decision diagrams (DDs) that provide outer approximations of MINLP feasible regions, we propose the concept of DD-free sets, which are convex regions whose interiors do not intersect the sets represented by the DDs. By exploiting the underlying graphical structure, we develop efficient methods for constructing these regions without requiring restrictive assumptions on the functional form of nonlinear constraints or access to distance oracles. We investigate the maximality properties of DD-free sets and devise algorithms for obtaining maximal forbidden regions within several structured classes. The resulting intersection cuts exploit geometric information retained in DD representations, enabling further strengthening of relaxations beyond what can be achieved through conventional DD-based convexification. We also introduce interval DDs to facilitate the representation of general nonlinear constraints and establish convergence results for intersections of constraint-specific DDs, providing a theoretical foundation for their integration into global optimization frameworks. Computational experiments on challenging open instances from MINLPLib, encompassing a broad range of nonlinear and nonconvex structures, demonstrate that the proposed approach can substantially improve dual bounds and achieve greater optimality-gap closure than state-of-the-art global optimization solvers. These findings highlight the potential of exploiting graphical representations of infeasible regions to develop stronger cutting planes for general MINLPs.

papers.title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
papers.abstract: We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $ν$-Schur functions. In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $ν$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data. Finally, we introduce $ν$-inner functions - $ν$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $ν$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $ν$-inner functions are dense in the $ν$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

papers.title: Pólya inequalities on thin planar networks
papers.abstract: We construct thin planar domains on which the Dirichlet and the Neumann Pólya inequalities both hold strictly. For the neighborhoods of a given finite connected embedded polygonal graph (branches and cycles are allowed) there is a single radius threshold below which both inequalities hold for every eigenvalue index. We also show that every nonempty bounded connected open set in the plane can be approximated, in measure and in the Hausdorff distance, by smooth simply connected domains satisfying both inequalities. Along the same sequence, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue tends to infinity, while each Neumann eigenvalue of fixed positive index tends to zero. In the special case of rectangular frames our estimates lead to explicit sufficient conditions, with no restriction on the aspect ratio.

papers.title: Monotonicity properties of ratios of Ferrers and conical functions related to a Riemannian nonlocal eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: Recently, for a given Riemannian manifold with certain curvature constraints, S. Kajántó and A. Kristály [KK24] formulated a variational problem (on either positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces) and computed the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in terms of the radii, curvature and weight. Moreover, they conjectured that a saturation phenomenon exists also in the case of positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces (not only in the Euclidean case), and this is based entirely on the incompatibility of a system of nonlinear equations involving special functions, like Ferrers functions of the first kind and conical functions of the first kind. In this paper, we provide a partial solution for both positive and negative curvature case.

papers.title: Advancing Quantum Reinforcement Learning with Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search and Adaptive Non-local Observables
papers.abstract: Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) using variational quantum circuits (VQCs) is constrained by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed circuit ansätze. Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANO) and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DiffQAS) address these issues independently, but to our knowledge have not been combined or compared in a single QRL framework. We present an ablation of ANO and DiffQAS within the Quantum Time-series Transformer (QTSTransformer), evaluated on a 2 x 2 factorial design across six environments--two classic-control tasks and four Atari 2600 games. Three findings emerge. First, the quantum agent outperforms a matched classical transformer baseline on five of six environments, with absolute scores ranging from 360.0 vs 304.0 (MarioBros) to 17.2 vs 2.5 (Breakout), while using approximately 12.5x fewer transformer parameters on the four Atari environments (more modestly so on the two classic-control tasks). Second, ANO and DiffQAS provide complementary benefits: ANO yields the largest gain on continuous-state CartPole (347.7 vs 223.2), while DiffQAS yields the largest absolute Atari gains (Breakout 17.2 vs 3.0; DonkeyKong 70.0 vs 37.0). Third, combining both innovations exhibits an asymmetric interaction: ANO-dominant tasks tolerate DiffQAS, whereas DiffQAS-dominant tasks degrade when ANO is added. These results provide design guidance for QRL agents: select between ANO and DiffQAS according to whether the bottleneck is the measurement basis or the gate topology, rather than applying both indiscriminately.

papers.title: Scalable and Interpretable Quantum Mixture of Experts for High-Dimensional Spatio-Temporal Data
papers.abstract: Quantum Mixture of Experts (QMoE) architectures offer a promising path toward scalable quantum machine learning, yet existing approaches remain largely confined to low-dimensional benchmarks and often rely on naive input partitioning that disrupts feature dependencies. We address these gaps by introducing Feature-Partitioned QMoE, which partitions high-dimensional spatio-temporal inputs into functionally coherent feature groups and assigns each group to a dedicated quantum expert. We further propose a hierarchical interpretability framework that leverages the modular structure of QMoE to produce circuit-level gating analysis, per-expert gradient saliency, and heterogeneity-based subtype discovery. Applied to ADHD classification from resting-state fMRI (N=4,458, ABCD Study, 180 brain ROIs, 363 timepoints), the proposed Theory-Driven QMoE achieves performance comparable to matched-capacity classical and quantum baselines while enabling circuit-attributable interpretation. The framework identifies FDR-corrected ADHD-associated biomarkers in executive-control and anterior default-mode networks and reveals three neurobiologically meaningful ADHD subtypes. These results position Feature-Partitioned QMoE as a scalable and interpretable methodology for applying quantum machine learning to high-dimensional biomedical data.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

papers.title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for $K_5$-minor-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gallai conjectured that the edges of every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. We prove that every connected $K_5$-minor-free graph other than $K_3$ and $K_5-e$ admits such a partition into at most $\floor{n/2}$ paths. The two exceptions require $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. In a smallest counterexample we find a $4$-connected planar part containing four vertices of degree five. Their neighborhoods meet the boundary in at most one vertex. This allows us to apply the planar configurations of Blanché, Bonamy, and Bonichon and to realize the reduced graph as a minor of the original graph.

papers.title: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

papers.title: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.

papers.title: Mean-field Token Steering
papers.abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schrödinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

papers.title: Simulated Annealing with Topological Spatial Chunking for De Novo Protein Sequence Design
papers.abstract: The inverse protein folding problem, designing a discrete amino acid sequence that spontaneously folds into a predefined macroscopic structure, remains a phenomenally demanding combinatorial challenge central to synthetic drug discovery. While algorithms like SA offer a baseline approach for navigating dense biomolecular energy landscapes, applying SA heuristics to large sequences is inherently frustrated by exponentially large search spaces and deep local energy minima. This study proposes a scalable sequence design architecture, Topological Spatial Chunking Simulated Annealing, based on a localized, exact-solving heuristic embedded within a global simulated-annealing wrapper. To fundamentally circumvent exponential scaling walls, we deploy a dynamic solver that segments the global molecular target into shallow, k-variable algorithmic windows. Crucially, rather than partitioning natively by sequential 1D chronology, we introduce topological spatial chunking, which dynamically groups discrete variables based on Euclidean spatial proximity to preserve critical non-local thermodynamic correlations. The spatially localized sub-problems are solved deterministically via exact enumeration, while the global traversal is securely regulated by an exterior simulated annealing governor augmented by dynamic reheating and continuous elitism caching. We comprehensively benchmarked this classical architecture on the standard HP biophysical lattice against targeted 20-merA, 25-mer, 50-mer, and 64-mer geometries. Most notably, when evaluating the computationally exhaustive 50-mer and 64-mer topologies, the framework successfully bypassed widely accepted heuristic boundaries. By leveraging deterministic exact solving to vault classical energy traps, the system algorithmically resolved a novel, ultra-dense sequence-packing configuration for the 50-mer, defining a new theoretical global optimum.

papers.title: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear Kirchhoff equation on the waveguide manifolds $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n$: \begin{align*} -\left( a+b \int_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n}|\nabla_{x,y}u(x,y)|^2\,dxdy\right) Δ_{x,y}u+ωu=|u|^αu, \end{align*} where $a,b>0$, $ω\in \mathbb{R}$, $α\in(0,2^*)$. We first establish existence of the normalized ground states when $α\in(0,2^*)$. To precisely characterize the $y$-dependence of ground states, we apply a scaling argument to handle the integral term $ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^n} |\nabla_{x,y} u(x,y)|^2 dxdy$. To this end, we construct two distinct modified energy functionals, through which we establish the $y$-independence and $y$-dependence of the ground states in two specific regimes: $(i)$ $ d + n \leq 4$ and $α\in (0, \frac{8}{d+n})$; $(ii)$ $d = n = 1$ and $α\in (8, \infty)$.

papers.title: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$.
